content:
{{Transcript|item}}

===<u>Chapter 1: Crystal Seed</u>===
As you may know, all crystal equipment is grown from a crystal seed. You may not know that all crystal seeds come from the same place; Tarddiad, the ancestral homeworld of the elves.

Reading the 'Cerddi' tells us that crystal seeds are sentient, although no one has ever been able converse with any crystal consciousness other than that of Seren herself.

One of the ways we can see this consciousness in action is in the way that crystal equipment, when first used, becomes aligned to that person.

===<u>Chapter 2: Crystal Chanting</u>===
As far as we can tell there have always been those with the ability to chant crystal, these tend to be from the Ithell clan, but it has been known for these 'Crystal Chanters' to be born to other clans as well.

The thing that makes 'Crystal Chanters' special is their ability to vocalise perfect pitches.

The idea behind chanting is quite simple: different pitches can change the shape and size of any facet of the seed. This allows a practiced chanter to make any number of shapes.

It is also possible for particularly gifted individuals to imbue powers into these objects. The only problem with this process is that it is very costly and time consuming.

The process can, however, be made more economical: the better the chanter knows the person for whom they are creating items, the easier it is to make.

===<u>Chapter 3: Crystal Properties</u>===
Although crystal seeds are highly convenient, they do have some drawbacks, the foremost of these is their brittleness.

This means that crystal equipment will eventually revert back to its original form, that of the crystal seed. However, crystal seeds can be reused to create new crystal equipment. Some equipment can also be reinforced to slow degradation.

Crystal seeds are among our most valuable assets, but with us unable to return to our homeworld since the loss of the World Gate, access to this resource has been lost. Luckily, there is no known way to fully destroy a crystal seed.

Transcript:Curator Herminius
content:
{{Transcript|npc}}

==Standard dialogue==
* '''Player:''' Hello.
* '''Curator:''' Nilsal to you, iknami. Welcome to the Grand Museum. I hope your visit is a pleasant one. If you have any questions about Varlamore, I'm happy to help.
* {{tselect|Select an Option}}
* {{topt|Could you tell me more about the early history of Varlamore?}}
** '''Player:''' Could you tell me more about the early history of Varlamore?
** '''Curator:''' Certainly! When it comes to the existence of Varlamore, it is Xeric we have to thank. During his Age of Strife, many refugees fled Kourend over the previously unexplored Custodia Mountains.
** '''Curator:''' There were three notable groups of these refugees. The first group, the Talkasti, settled in the Tlati Rainforest.
** '''Curator:''' While they initially lived nomadic lives, they eventually started to establish more permanent settlements, with Tal Teklan being the first.
** '''Curator:''' The next group were the Pericans. They first settled right here, building the town of Fortis, or Civitas illa Fortis as it eventually became.
** '''Curator:''' Finally we have the dwarves. These were refugees from Lovakengj who established a home beneath Ralos' Rise, becoming known as the Dwarves of Cam Torum.
** '''Player:''' Was there any friction between these groups initially?
** '''Curator:''' Oh yes, very much so. The dwarves, just as they do today, mostly kept to themselves. However, the Talkasti and Pericans came into regular conflict over various matters.
** '''Player:''' But that's not the case now, right? What brought them together?
** '''Curator:''' As you may well have already guessed, it was religion. Long before leaving Kourend, the Talkasti had taken to secretly worshipping Ralos and Ranul.
** '''Curator:''' After arriving here, they were able to openly practice their religion for the first time. Over time, the Pericans started to adopt this religion as well.
** '''Curator:''' As the two groups came together, the population of the region started to rapidly expand. This eventually led to the construction of Tempestus, and with it, the founding of Varlamore.
** '''Player:''' So are there still distinctions between the Talkasti and the Pericans now?
** '''Curator:''' Yes and no. Those terms are no longer used to describe people today. Since we united, we have all been Varlamorians. However, you'll still find many traces of our previous divide.
** '''Curator:''' For example, here in Fortis, you'll find yourself surrounded by Perican architecture, whereas over in the Tlati Rainforest, the influence of the Talkasti remains clear.
** '''Curator:''' Names are another good example. Indeed, look no further than our rulers. For most of our history, we were ruled by the Tullus dynasty, with Tullus very much being a name of Perican origin.
** '''Curator:''' However, we are now ruled by the Arkan dynasty, whose name can be traced back to early Talkasti nomads.
** '''Player:''' I see. So where did the name Varlamore come from.
** '''Curator:''' The name comes from the River Varla that separated Talkasti and Perican territory. What was once a symbol of our divide, became the symbol of our unification.
** '''Player:''' That was all super interesting! Thanks for the information.
** '''Curator:''' Not a problem, iknami!
** {{tselect|Select an Option}}
** {{topt|Could you tell me more about religion in Varlamore?}}
*** {{tact|below}}
** {{topt|Could you tell me more about Varlamore's recent history?}}
*** {{tact|below}}
** {{topt|I'd better get going. Thanks again.}}
*** '''Player:''' I'd better get going. Thanks again.
*** {{tact|end}}
* {{topt|Could you tell me more about religion in Varlamore?}}
** '''Player:''' Could you tell me more about religion in Varlamore?
** '''Curator:''' Of course! Whereas in other parts of the world you'll likely find followers of many gods, here in Varlamore, you'll only really find those dedicated to Ralos and Ranul.
** '''Curator:''' Losanium is the official term for this religion, though it is not a term you'll find used very often.
** '''Player:''' How come?
** '''Curator:''' Losanium encompasses the worship of both Ralos and Ranul, and while they do indeed go hand in hand, it is rare to find individuals equally dedicated to both.
** '''Curator:''' Instead, most people focus their worship on one of the two, with Ralos being by far the more popular. Something that isn't too surprising given Ranul's association with death.
** '''Curator:''' Now that said, you might actually find a higher than normal number of Ranul worshippers right here in the museum.
** '''Curator:''' Something that is easily forgotten is that while Ranul is indeed a god of death, he is also a god of learning and knowledge.
** '''Curator:''' If you wish to learn more, you may well want to seek out one of the teoki in the temple to the south. Though of course, they may well have somewhat biased takes on their religious practices.
** '''Player:''' I'll keep that in mind. Thanks.
** '''Curator:''' Don't mention it.
** {{tact|other}}
* {{topt|Could you tell me more about Varlamore's recent history?}}
** '''Player:''' Could you tell me more about Varlamore's recent history?
** '''Curator:''' I can indeed! When it comes to recent events in the kingdom, the best place to start is with the War of Betrayal. It all started around 100 years ago when Imafore Tullus ascended to the throne.
** '''Curator:''' He soon reorganised the kingdom into the Varlamorian Empire, a controversial choice to say the least, though it soon became clear that controversial choices were quite popular with Imafore.
** '''Curator:''' While public opinion was always mixed, nothing he did resulted in outright conflict until his sudden and brutal murder of the Kourend Royal Family. War was quickly declared.
** '''Curator:''' Until that day, Varlamore had successfully managed to avoid conflict since before the kingdom was officially established. To say the war was unpopular would be an understatement.
** '''Curator:''' Imafore soon found himself facing as much resistance from within as he did from Kourend. The end result was predictable.
** '''Curator:''' Imafore and his forces found themselves trapped between two armies at the Battle of the Proudspire. He was captured and executed, bringing an end to the Tullus dynasty.
** '''Curator:''' This brings us to a fun little fact. After his death, Imafore was succeeded by King Mezpah Arkan. One of his first acts was to call for the beheading of every statue of Imafore in the kingdom.
** '''Curator:''' The statues remain to this day. It's actually a crime to try and remove them. They exist as a reminder of our history, and a warning to any who would try to follow in Imafore's footsteps.
** '''Player:''' I'll have to keep an eye out for them.
** '''Curator:''' Indeed. I often like to challenge people to try and find them all!
** '''Player:''' So how has the kingdom changed since Imafore died?
** '''Curator:''' The War of Betrayal was very much seen as a wake- up call. While Varlamore had once flourished under the traditions of the Tullus dynasty, by the end, it's fair to say we were stagnating.
** '''Curator:''' King Mezpah set to work on transforming the kingdom. His ambitions were high, to the point that much of what he desired never came to pass in his lifetime.
** '''Curator:''' One of his most notable goals was to see Varlamore open more widely to the outer world. A goal which thanks to his great-granddaughter, has now finally been achieved!
** '''Player:''' Well then I should be very thankful. Without him, I might never have been allowed to visit!
** '''Curator:''' Indeed. We would often send our students on trips to the east prior to the opening of the borders. The amount of paperwork needed was astounding! Now we can just hop on a ship any time we like!
** '''Player:''' That definitely sounds much more fun. Thanks for all the information.
** '''Curator:''' It's not a problem, iknami.
** {{tact|other}}
* {{topt|Thanks. If I have any questions, I'll be sure to ask.}}
** '''Player:''' Thanks. If I have any questions, I'll be sure to ask.
** {{tact|end}}

==Talking to Valdez==
* '''Player:''' Hello.
* '''Mysterious ghost:''' H-hello!
* '''Player:''' So what's up?
* '''Mysterious ghost:''' I cannot believe it! You can see me? You understand my words?
* '''Player:''' Sure can. So why are you hanging around here?
* '''Mysterious ghost:''' My tale is one of woe... No doubt you will have little interest in hearing it...
* '''Mysterious ghost:''' Though it has been so many moons since last I had company in this endless non-life...
* {{topt|Tell me your story}}
** '''Player:''' Well, actually I would like to know what happened to you to turn you into an invisible ghost.
** '''Player:''' If only so I can make sure it doesn't happen to me...
** '''Mysterious ghost:''' My name is Valdez. I served my Lord Saradomin faithfully for many years, as an explorer of this strange land we had been brought to.
** '''Mysterious ghost:''' I remember the day this curse fell upon me clearly... I had just discovered a huge temple, hidden below the ground, of one of Saradomin's compatriots.
** '''Mysterious ghost:''' I am unsure who had built it, or why they had left it seemingly abandoned, but inside I located a great treasure...

** '''Player:''' What, you mean you gave it to Saradomin and in return he cursed you???

** '''Player:''' And secondly?

** '''Mysterious ghost:''' The vile thief Rennard accosted me as I made my way to Entrana, and after defeating me with a sneak attack, plundered the staff from my person, and left me for dead...
** '''Mysterious ghost:''' I do not know what became of the staff, but I can feel in my very bones that whatever its final fate was, it is somehow related to this curse upon me...
** '''Player:''' Wow. Tough break.
** '''Mysterious ghost:''' I am sorry to bore you with my tale stranger, please allow me to compound my rudeness by asking you for one favour, small to perform?
** '''Player:''' Eh, I won't make any promises, but if it's nothing too annoying I guess I can help you out.
** '''Mysterious ghost:''' Many thanks stranger, this existence tortures me...
** '''Mysterious ghost:''' I need you to find Rennard and if he has the staff yet reclaim it, or find out what hideous deed he performed to curse me so!
** '''Mysterious ghost:''' I have nothing I may offer you save this piece of clothing, please take it as payment...
** '''Player:''' Where can I find this Rennard then?
** {{tcond|If Rennard is in the [[Bandit Camp (Wilderness)|Wilderness Bandit Camp]]:}}
*** '''Mysterious ghost:''' Ah, the infamous Rennard... The last I had heard of that vile thief, he had joined a group of bandits in an evil land to the North-east of here, where they had made their home living outside of
*** '''Mysterious ghost:''' the reach of the authorities that pursued them...

*** '''Player:''' Okay, well I'll try and find him for you then.
*** {{tact|end}}

*** '''Mysterious ghost:''' the desert awaiting the return of their dark master...

==Talking to Kharrim==
* '''Player:''' Hello. So you must be Kharrim the messenger.

* {{topt|Tell me your story}}

** '''Mysterious ghost:''' Well, if you have spoken to Rennard, then you will know that he had somehow managed to obtain a very valuable weapon, and was looking for buyers.
** '''Mysterious ghost:''' What he probably didn't tell you, was that he met me in a drunken stupor in some smoke filled tavern, and I offered to arrange a purchaser for his item, in exchange for a small finders fee.
** '''Player:''' So you knew what the staff was?

** '''Mysterious ghost:''' Honestly, you would have to be pretty slow-witted to not recognise a legendary artefact such as that.
** '''Player:''' Wait, I don't understand, Rennard said that he had a buyer already in mind, and that you diverted his message to a General Zamorak instead?
** '''Mysterious ghost:''' Ha! Here is a word of advice for you adventurer; Never trust the words of a drunk.
** '''Mysterious ghost:''' Whatever he might have thought he was doing with it, in the end all that happened was he left me to arrange a purchaser for the item.
** '''Player:''' So you thought you would offer it to General Zamorak?
** '''Mysterious ghost:''' Ah yes, Lord Zamorak. He was merely a mortal back then, you know?
** '''Mysterious ghost:''' Yet I could see great things in store for him even then. He had a kind of brilliant ruthlessness... And that special kind of vicious streak you see so rarely...
** '''Mysterious ghost:''' Well anyway, when given the task of selling a weapon forged by the very gods themselves, I naturally thought of Zamorak as a potential buyer.
** '''Mysterious ghost:''' I was a messenger in his employ anyway, so it was a mere trifle to find him and deliver the news, and I knew of his particular interest in armour and weaponry of all kinds.
** '''Mysterious ghost:''' Yes, he was always quite the connoisseur when it came to weaponry...
** '''Mysterious ghost:''' But I digress. I let Lord Zamorak know that there was some drunken fool with an artefact of incredible power that could probably be bought off with a few jewels and trinkets,
** '''Mysterious ghost:''' and he escorted me to the tavern and made the purchase there and then.
** '''Mysterious ghost:''' It was a satisfactory deal all around, I got a share of the sale price from Rennard, and I greatly increased my prestige amongst Zamorak and his followers.
** '''Mysterious ghost:''' But maybe... Perhaps the events that followed were responsible for my cursed state...
** '''Player:''' Events that followed?
** '''Mysterious ghost:''' I can not tell you of them precisely, for I myself was not there to witness them.
** '''Mysterious ghost:''' I am after all, simply a messenger. When... 'it' happened, I was busy elsewhere delivering a message from Zamorak to the rest of his Mahjarrat ilk.
** '''Player:''' When 'it' happened? What was 'it'?
** '''Mysterious ghost:''' As I have explained, I was not there, and I do not know what Zamorak did with the staff, but whatever it was resulted in his banishment by the other gods for many years.
** '''Mysterious ghost:''' The very strange thing was that Saradomin must have known about it, whatever it was, before it even happened...
** '''Player:''' Really? Why do you say that?
** '''Mysterious ghost:''' Well, it was the contents of the message I was returning to Zamorak;
** '''Mysterious ghost:''' Lucien seemed quite certain that there was a spy for Saradomin somewhere amongst his followers named Lennissa.
** '''Mysterious ghost:''' If whatever happened to the staff caused this curse to befall me, then it is certain that she too would have been afflicted, because she would have been in the very heart of the action.
** '''Mysterious ghost:''' Hmmm....
** '''Mysterious ghost:''' You have given me much to think on adventurer. I would like to reward you with my sturdy messenger boots, may they aid you in your travels.

** '''Mysterious ghost:''' Ah yes, the whereabouts of the treacherous Lennissa...

* '''Player:''' Hello. You would be Lennissa, I take it?

* {{topt|Tell me your story}}
** '''Player:''' Then please, go ahead and tell me the events of that day in your own words...
** '''Mysterious ghost:''' Let me see... I had been working as a spy for my Lord Saradomin, amongst the forces of... the Empty Lord.
** '''Player:''' 'The Empty Lord'? Who is that?
** '''Mysterious ghost:''' I will not give you his name, for to do so would give him power here.
** '''Mysterious ghost:''' Let us just say that he was a fearsome deity, whose strength was greater than all the gods we knew of on this realm at the time.
** '''Mysterious ghost:''' It is probably worth mentioning that at this time we had no knowledge of the mysterious nature god Guthix.
** '''Player:''' So he was stronger than Saradomin?
** '''Mysterious ghost:''' As Saradomin was, yes. As Saradomin is now? Who can say?
** '''Player:''' I see... Please, continue.
** '''Mysterious ghost:''' As I say, I was working as a spy within the very camp of my Lord's enemies.
** '''Mysterious ghost:''' I knew that should I have been caught, I risked being killed upon the spot, but my combat skills were always formidable, and if truth be told, there was a fair amount of dissent amongst... 'his' followers anyway.
** '''Player:''' How do you mean 'dissent'?
** '''Mysterious ghost:''' Ah, to not understand this, you must have led a sheltered life...
** '''Mysterious ghost:''' Let me tell you this: Evil will always breed more evil, and will never be satisfied with what it has.
** '''Mysterious ghost:''' The Empty Lord chose to ally himself with the dark creatures of this world, fully aware that their own natures would cause them to rally against his rule, and take every opportunity they could to betray him.
** '''Mysterious ghost:''' This has always been the nature of evil. Perhaps he thought his power could prevent such treachery?
** '''Mysterious ghost:''' This allowed me freedom amongst their camp, for it was always easy to point the finger of suspicion at some unsuspecting necromancer or foolish Mahjarrat if it seemed as though my activities had been discovered.
** '''Mysterious ghost:''' Similarly, should I ever be caught in the act of my sabotage, it was all too easy to bribe whoever found me or persuade them into believing it was just some minor treachery of my own, rather than my work for my
** '''Mysterious ghost:''' Lord Saradomin.
** '''Player:''' Okay... Well, that makes sense, but I don't understand what the Staff of Armadyl had to do with this...?
** '''Mysterious ghost:''' As I have told you, the Empty Lord was extremely powerful, but not so powerful that he could rule over the other deities of this world without opposition.
** '''Mysterious ghost:''' Should he have made a move against any other god, then he could still have been easily brought down by the combined efforts of the others.
** '''Mysterious ghost:''' The theft of Armadyl's staff changed this however.
** '''Mysterious ghost:''' If he had taken possession of this god-weapon, then his power would have been so great that he could have overthrown all on this world, and made it into his own image!
** '''Mysterious ghost:''' I could not allow such a thing to happen!
** '''Mysterious ghost:''' I went immediately to my comrade Dhalak, the mage, and told him that a message had come to the lair offering this weapon for sale!
** '''Mysterious ghost:''' I knew that as soon as my Lord Saradomin heard this, he would contact Armadyl to inform them of the theft, and the matter would have been resolved quickly and discreetly.
** '''Player:''' So you passed this information to Dhalak instead of taking it to Saradomin yourself?
** '''Mysterious ghost:''' To my eternal shame, I indeed failed my Lord Saradomin...
** '''Mysterious ghost:''' I could not risk taking the message directly, for I feared my disguise had been uncovered.
** '''Mysterious ghost:''' Lucien particularly had been taking an unhealthy interest in my activities, and I had a gut feeling that to make any obvious moves against the Empty Lord would have been my undoing.
** '''Mysterious ghost:''' But Dhalak was a noble man! I cannot believe that he would not have taken my message immediately to Lord Saradomin!
** '''Player:''' Well, it seems like he didn't, but I don't know why not...
** '''Mysterious ghost:''' Please adventurer, discover what foul fate must have befallen him for him to have neglected his duty!
** '''Mysterious ghost:''' I have not much to offer as reward, but for these spare robes I wore while on assignment...
** '''Mysterious ghost:''' Please find him and discover why I am cursed like this!

** '''Mysterious ghost:''' there was a growing faction amongst them who were plotting to overthrow their master.

** '''Mysterious ghost:''' being a god-weapon its very presence would have sung out to their leader.

** '''Mysterious ghost:''' Indeed I did. To my eternal shame, I decided that I would assist Zamorak and his henchmen in their battle, by secretly casting a spell of concealment upon the staff so that
** '''Mysterious ghost:''' they might use it secretly against their master.
** '''Player:''' So Zamorak knew about this?
** '''Mysterious ghost:''' No, nobody except myself, and now you, knew that I cast such a spell....
** '''Mysterious ghost:''' Had I known what a threat to my Lord Saradomin Zamorak would later become, I wouldst have taken the message to Saradomin immediately! Alas, it is all too easy to see your mistakes after you
** '''Mysterious ghost:''' have made them...
** '''Player:''' I'm confused. What exactly happened with this staff anyway? And why have all these various random people been cursed because of it?
** '''Mysterious ghost:''' I cannot answer your question with anything other than my own suppositions, but I do know of one who might be able to, and if any man deserved to be cursed for their actions that day, it was he!
** '''Player:''' Who are you speaking of?
** '''Mysterious ghost:''' His name was Viggora. He was an evil man, brutal and vicious, and deadly with a blade.
** '''Mysterious ghost:''' He was one of the few humans Zamorak allowed to rise to a position of power amongst his rebels, possibly because he imitated those same qualities of Zamorak.
** '''Mysterious ghost:''' If anyone knows what Zamorak did with that god- weapon to have caused this curse to have befallen us, it would have been he, for he would have been fighting on Zamorak's very right hand side in their rebellion.
** '''Mysterious ghost:''' Please, if this curse can be lifted, find Viggora and find out what he has wrought upon us! I have no wealth nor magic to aid you, but take my hood as reward;
** '''Mysterious ghost:''' it has served me well these centuries past, and may bring you luck.
** '''Player:''' Where would you suggest I look for Viggora?
** {{tcond|If Viggora is in the [[Rogues' Castle]]:}}
*** '''Mysterious ghost:''' Ah, the evil swordsman Viggora... A rogue like him would probably flock to his own kind.
*** '''Player:''' Okay, well I'll try and find him for you then.
*** {{tact|end}}
** {{tcond|If Viggora is in the [[Slayer Tower]]:}}

*** '''Player:''' Okay, well I'll try and find him for you then.

*** {{tact|end}}

==Talking to Viggora==
* '''Player:''' So... You must be the infamous Viggora.
* '''Mysterious ghost:''' Hold thy tongue varlet! Speak fast, how come you to find me here, and how doth you understand mine speech?
* '''Player:''' You want me to hold my tongue and tell you how I found you?
* '''Mysterious ghost:''' Cease thy chatter and respond to my demand!
* '''Player:''' Cease my chatter AND respond to your demand?
* '''Mysterious ghost:''' I warn thee knave, this curse upon me hath not improved my temper, these centuries past...
* '''Player:''' Well, it's actually about that curse that I have come to speak to you.
* '''Mysterious ghost:''' Oh, be that so? Then forgive my swift anger, and speak to me of how you plan to break this curse.
* '''Player:''' Erm... I didn't actually mention anything about breaking the curse...
* '''Mysterious ghost:''' Then what lets you dare speak to me?
* '''Player:''' Well, I heard of your name from a mage called Dhalak, and I'm trying to find out what exactly caused the curse to befall him, and you as well apparently.
* '''Mysterious ghost:''' Ha! So the weak-willed mage was cursed along with me?
* '''Mysterious ghost:''' Well now, that is an interesting turn of events... Then am I to assume that Valdez, Rennard, Kharrim and Lennissa were also cursed along with me?
* '''Player:''' ...How did you know that?
* '''Mysterious ghost:''' Ha ha ha! Oh, the curse cut deeper than I had previously thought!
* '''Mysterious ghost:''' Stranger, this news has brought me a ray of sunshine in an otherwise dreary millennium! Please, ask any question you wish!
* {{topt|Tell me your story}}
** '''Player:''' Erm... Thanks, I think. So what exactly happened on that day you were all cursed?
** '''Player:''' I know that Valdez discovered the Staff of Armadyl, was robbed by Rennard, who then sent Kharrim to tell Zamorak of it.
** '''Player:''' Meanwhile Lennissa heard of the sale, and informed Dhalak who placed an enchantment upon it so that its power would be hidden.
** '''Player:''' I still don't know what happened with the staff to cause this curse, or what you had to do with it though...
** '''Mysterious ghost:''' Well stranger, rest yourself awhile, and I will recount a tale of the events of that day, for I was one of the few actually there when it happened...
** '''Player:''' When what happened?
** '''Mysterious ghost:''' When my Lord Zamorak first got his taste of godhood!
** '''Player:''' Wow. Sounds like quite the dinner party anecdote.
** '''Mysterious ghost:''' You can take the snide venom out of your voice whelp, you came to me; 'twas not the other way round.
** '''Player:''' Okay, okay. Please continue.
** '''Mysterious ghost:''' Well now, let us see... As you may have heard tell, my affiliation lay with General Zamorak, a mighty warrior of the Mahjarrat tribe, and my skill on the battlefield had quickly brought
** '''Mysterious ghost:''' me to his attention.
** '''Mysterious ghost:''' So pleased was he with my bloodlust that he promoted me on the battlefield once to serve in his honour guard, and let me tell you, this was a rare honour indeed, for I was the only human chosen to take such a position.
** '''Player:''' Really?
** '''Mysterious ghost:''' Oh yes, the dragon riders, Mahjarrat, demons and vampyre warriors made up the bulk of the force, but I wager I was their equal in all ways of combat.
** '''Mysterious ghost:''' Ha, when I think of someone like Lucien struggling to lift a blade, in some ways I was even their better!
** '''Player:''' Please continue.
** '''Mysterious ghost:''' Well anyway... Myself and the rest of Zamoraks honour guard were formulating stratagems in our battle-tent, when that sneaky messenger Kharrim came in offering to sell us
** '''Mysterious ghost:''' the god-staff of Armadyl!
** '''Mysterious ghost:''' Naturally, we suspected that this was some trick by our Lord to test our loyalty...
** '''Player:''' Yes, who was your lord? Everyone has been very evasive about that...
** '''Mysterious ghost:''' Quiet fool, all things in their course; You are disrupting my train of thought!
** '''Player:''' Sorry...
** '''Mysterious ghost:''' Well anyway, we thought it was too good to be true, yet when we visited this scummy tavern we were amazed to discover there was no trick, no test of loyalty, no hidden trap:
** '''Mysterious ghost:''' Somehow this fool had actually managed to obtain the god-staff of Armadyl!
** '''Mysterious ghost:''' Its power was incredible, you could almost feel the energies crackling around it in the air!
** '''Player:''' So what happened then?
** '''Mysterious ghost:''' Well, with such a weapon, the plans we had been developing for a rebellion against our lord could finally be put into action, but we knew that we would have to act swiftly, before he heard that we had a weapon
** '''Mysterious ghost:''' capable of defeating him, and we would have to act decisively, for even amongst our group there were still those loyal to the lord - such as that pathetic fool Azzanadra.
** '''Player:''' So JUST WHO WAS this lord you speak of?
** '''Mysterious ghost:''' And I tell thee again, I will say when it is appropriate, now do not disrupt my tale!
** '''Player:''' Okay, carry on then...
** '''Mysterious ghost:''' So anyway, Lord Zamorak and his most trusted compatriots, namely myself, Hazeel, Drakan, Thammaron and Zemouregal made plans to overthrow our lord using the god-weapon, and by pledging
** '''Mysterious ghost:''' allegiance to Zamorak as our master, were each to be given a large piece of land as our own in return.
** '''Mysterious ghost:''' We decided to move immediately, before anyone got cold feet, or any other parties could interfere in our work, and made haste towards the castle where our Lord lived.
** '''Mysterious ghost:''' If Lucien had not been otherwise occupied, he would have probably accompanied us with his magicks, but it turned out the foolish Dhalak had made his involvement unnecessary with some spells of his own allowing us to
** '''Mysterious ghost:''' get close enough to the castle with the staff without the Empty Lord being able to sense its presence.
** '''Player:''' So your lord was the one that cursed you?
** '''Mysterious ghost:''' I am coming to that... So anyway, we made our way to the castle, under the pretense that we had war plans against Saradomin and the other deities to discuss.
** '''Mysterious ghost:''' As usual, our lord was guarded well, but this was why Zamorak had brought his most trusted fighters with him.
** '''Mysterious ghost:''' While we distracted the Empty Lord with our feints and attacks, and kept his bodyguards busy, Lord Zamorak outflanked him, unsheathed the staff and plunged it into his back!
** '''Mysterious ghost:''' Ah, it was a glorious sight... At that moment I was reminded for whom I fought, and why General Zamorak had earned his nickname 'the scourge' upon the battlefield...
** '''Player:''' And the next thing you know you were cursed?
** '''Mysterious ghost:''' No, it was not quite that simple... The Empty Lord turned away from our battle, eyes burning with hatred, and towards Zamorak instead. Seeing this, we all fought with extra vigour, so that
** '''Mysterious ghost:''' General Zamorak would not face our lord alone, but we were outnumbered by many hundreds of warriors and demons, and could not reach him to assist him!
** '''Player:''' So what then?
** '''Mysterious ghost:''' Why, it was the Empty Lord versus Zamorak, in single combat! And the sight of the battle will be with me forever more...
** '''Mysterious ghost:''' The Empty Lord was a powerful god, stronger than any of the others awake at that time, possibly even as strong as Guthix is, and Zamorak was but a mortal: A Mahjarrat warrior all the same, with all of the
** '''Mysterious ghost:''' strength and power that that entails, but mortal nonetheless, but to see him fight, you would not think of him as a 'mere' anything...
** '''Mysterious ghost:''' He was war itself! Flurry after flurry of blows he rained upon the Empty Lord, and the very castle walls shook and quivered with their power, but the Empty Lord would not fall!
** '''Mysterious ghost:''' Even with the weapon of a god embedded in his back, he fought on, and with each blow our victory seemed less and less certain...
** '''Player:''' So what then?
** '''Mysterious ghost:''' Well, then a miracle happened. Or luck. Or natural justice.
** '''Mysterious ghost:''' You can call it what you want, but as the Empty Lords hands wrapped tightly around Zamorak's throat, Lord Zamorak, kicking and screaming defiantly and radiant in his anger until the very last, plunged towards the
** '''Mysterious ghost:''' Empty Lord, who seemed to lose his footing slightly, and fell in such a way so that the staff plunged deeper into his body, but also impaled Lord Zamorak with it at the same time...
** '''Mysterious ghost:''' And then...
** '''Player:''' And then what?
** '''Mysterious ghost:''' And then nothing. There was a sudden flash of bright light, and then a sudden blink of cold darkness, and it was over.
** '''Mysterious ghost:''' Zamorak stood over the Empty Lord who was slowly... fading from existence... And as he faded, it seemed as though... It almost seemed as though Zamorak became more real,
** '''Mysterious ghost:''' more solid than he had been before...
** '''Mysterious ghost:''' And as the Empty Lord faded from this world completely, I heard his voice, almost a whisper upon the wind, cursing all who had helped Zamorak in his victory, which as you now tell me seems to have been all who
** '''Mysterious ghost:''' were responsible for the staff ending up in Zamorak's hands at the castle.
** '''Mysterious ghost:''' As I heard it, I saw that I too was fading, just as the Empty Lord had, and I called to my brethren for their assistance, but they could no longer hear my words, nor see my form.
** '''Mysterious ghost:''' It was then that the other gods appeared and banished Zamorak from the world completely for daring to kill one of their kind, although as it turned out it didn't quite work out that way for them, when he returned
** '''Mysterious ghost:''' stronger than ever, a god himself.
** '''Mysterious ghost:''' But the god wars were another story entirely...
** '''Player:''' But... I don't understand... If it was Zamorak who used the weapon, then why was it only you who were cursed?
** '''Player:''' And the other people who were cursed, why them? Why not the other Mahjarrat for example?
** '''Player:''' And just who was this 'Empty Lord' you keep speaking of?
** '''Mysterious ghost:''' Well, in my life I was nothing but a warrior. I had no hidden knowledge, I didn't especially care about the gods or their magics, and I certainly didn't respect them.
** '''Mysterious ghost:''' Now in my... I suppose this is my death. I am but a shade on the wind, unnoticed by all who pass me, until today anyway, and the only answer I can give you is that the others who were with me, the
** '''Mysterious ghost:''' Mahjarrats and the Vampyre, they were beings of magic.
** '''Mysterious ghost:''' It runs through their very veins, and ebbs through their bones.
** '''Mysterious ghost:''' Who knows why the curse fell as it did? Perhaps as a mere human I was more susceptible to it, when they were not. Perhaps they too are cursed, but their life spans are so
** '''Mysterious ghost:''' long that it will be millennia before they feel it upon them. Perhaps because it did not affect them, it extended backwards through time, to the moment the staff was
** '''Mysterious ghost:''' taken from its rightful place, and all who had known of its theft were cursed too. Perhaps there are others also cursed, who played no part in this tale, and were merely unlucky enough to be
** '''Mysterious ghost:''' in the wrong place at the wrong time...
** '''Mysterious ghost:''' I don't know. Things do not always happen for a reason, just as tales do not always end with all of the loose ends neatly tied up and all answers supplied.
** '''Mysterious ghost:''' I have simply told you the events I was witness to, for I can do no more.
** '''Mysterious ghost:''' You have cheered me no end to let me know that this curse that has afflicted me has not left me alone here, in this void between worlds.
** '''Mysterious ghost:''' Perhaps I will hunt down these others who have also been cursed as I was, but I feel I must reward you for your efforts; Here, take my cloak, it is drenched in the blood of a
** '''Mysterious ghost:''' thousand foes, and may bring you luck in battle.
** '''Player:''' So how can I break this curse?
** '''Mysterious ghost:''' Who knows? If it was the death curse of the Empty Lord, there may be no way to break it.
** '''Mysterious ghost:''' If it was not his death curse, and he is still alive but not on this world, then the only way to break it may be to bring him back here;
** '''Mysterious ghost:''' But I would rather stay cursed than suffer under his rule again...
** '''Player:''' But WHO was this 'Empty Lord'? WHAT was his NAME?
** '''Mysterious ghost:''' You do not know? You have not guessed yet?
** '''Mysterious ghost:''' He was Zaros.
** {{tact|end}}
* {{topt|Goodbye then}}
** '''Player:''' Well, that's all fascinating, but I just don't particularly care. Bye-bye.
** {{tact|end}}

===Talking to Viggora again===
* '''Player:''' Hello.
* '''Mysterious ghost:''' Hello yourself.
* {{topt|Talk about Viggora's story.}}
** '''Player:''' I really liked your little story. Can you tell me another one?
** '''Player:''' Preferably something with a big fight and lots of explosions!
** '''Mysterious ghost:''' ...You are a very strange young [man/woman].
** {{tact|end}}
* {{topt|Ask for more ghostly robes.}}
** '''Player:''' Could I have more of those ghostly robes you gave me?
** '''Mysterious ghost:''' It seems as though the curse that keeps me here extends to my very clothing... which piece do you want?
** {{tact|opens2=Ghostly robes reclaim interface}}
** {{tact|receives=the requested piece(s) of [[ghostly robes]]}}
** '''Mysterious ghost:''' Here you go.
** {{tact|end}}

Transcript:Dagon'hai history
content:
{{Transcript|item}}

'...In scarred lands and ruined fields, that circle flaming towers high, where cruel and cursed torments yield, the Dark of Man, the Dagon'hai.'

'The Prophecies of Zamorak'

...until the day that the Zamorakian Magi were welcomed among the human numbers. The Zamorakian numbers grew and some moved their order to the city of Varrock. These were the Dagon'hai.

The practices of the Dagon'hai were looked darkly upon by the priests of Saradomin within the walls of Varrock and, thus, the Dagon'hai were forced into a hidden war, away from the eyes of the citizens of Varrock.

Priests of Saradomin were found dead in darkened streets and crumbling houses. Dagon'hai were cast into cells and tormented through purification. Varrock was torn between the followers of two warring deities. Yet, the people of Varrock did nothing...

...until the tower fell. The famed Wizards' Tower in the south burned for what seemed like an age and the people of Varrock knew they had been misled. They turned upon the Zamorakian mages with murderous intent and the Dagon'hai, even with their skills in dark wizardry, were unable to confront such a vengeance-filled assault against their order, supported in full by the priests of Saradomin.

The Dagon'hai were all but decimated. Their numbers were shattered and they hid themselves in the darkest houses in the most dimly lit of streets within the city. Those that survived the exodus delved deeper into the most evil of arcane magic, intent on exacting retribution upon the priests of Saradomin and the people of Varrock.

Varrock may have fallen if not for the purest of chances. A young guardsman on patrol in the city happened across a dimly lit house in a corner of the city. Sensing something evil in the air, he cautiously peered through one of the small windows and was aghast to see the High Elders of the Dagon'hai engaged in a sacrificial ritual. Sounding the alarm, the guard called for help and the Dagon'hai, knowing they would be slaughtered, fled into the night.

The last remaining Dagon'hai were chased throughout Varrock to the great statue of Saradomin himself. Then, they all but disappeared. Nobody knows what happened to them, but some say they were set upon by creatures from the Wilderness. Others say that they teleported themselves away to a place of safety. A few claimed they saw men disappearing into the earth beneath the statue itself. It was as though the statue of Saradomin had claimed their lives in his name.

The Dagon'hai never reappeared in Varrock, yet the people knew that one day they would return to have their revenge.

title: Transcript:Dakh'thoulan Aegis
content:
{{Transcript|npc}}

==Standard dialogue==
* '''Player:''' Hi there.
* '''Dakh'thoulan Aegis:''' Hello, young one. What brings you to our humble dwelling?
* '''Player:''' I was wondering what this place was?
* '''Dakh'thoulan Aegis:''' These are the Tunnels of Chaos. They radiate with the energy of chaos magic. At the far end of the tunnel, you will find a portal to the Chaos Altar itself where chaos runes are crafted!
* {{topt|Why is the tunnel so short?}}
** '''Player:''' Why is the tunnel so short?
** '''Dakh'thoulan Aegis:''' The nature of chaos magic itself is mysterious and hard to understand.
** '''Player:''' What do you mean?
** '''Dakh'thoulan Aegis:''' The tunnel is here, and yet it is not here. We also are here, where we should be, yet we are somewhere else. And so, the tunnel goes from one place to another, yet touches neither.
** '''Player:''' I really don't understand.
** '''Dakh'thoulan Aegis:''' I told you you wouldn't. The best way to think of it is that the tunnel is like a gateway that allows you to travel from one place in the world to another in a more safe and convenient way.
** '''Player:''' Oh, I think I see. So it is like a magical alternate route?

** '''Player:''' Oh, ok.

content:
{{No official name|Jagex didn't give this Postbag a name.}}
{{Postbag|issue=26|date=28 January 2022|url=https://secure.runescape.com/m=news/gielinor-gazette---january-2022?oldschool=1|osrs=yes}}
{{Transcript list|Messenger (The Frozen Door){{!}}Messenger|Nechryael|My Arm|Pontak|Skotizo|Konar quo Maten|Observatory professor|noplayer}}

New Year, New Postbag! This year my resolution is to deliver even more of your lovely letters, in rain, heat, snow, or gloom of night! It shouldn't be too hard, since most of Gielinor doesn't have weather. Ha ha!

Anyway, let's take a look at this month's post!

----
==To the [[Messenger (The Frozen Door)|Messenger]]==
{{Letter|To the extremely persistent Messenger,

I know you're scared of your employer, but trying to pass that letter to me at the bottom of the ocean seems a bit much. Have you thought about a less hazardous use of your talents? Maybe delivering Gnomish cuisine?

Signed, a slightly concerned adventurer}}

What on Gielinor is this?!

I was just minding my own business and this blooming talking skull popped out of nowhere and handed me a letter! What if I'd been in the bath or something?

Hmm.

In hindsight I may have been a bit overzealous. But you have to understand, the sender of that letter was not to be trifled with! I'm just glad the whole ordeal is over.

I'm not sure what I'll do now, although your friend Pete here says the GPDT are always looking for talented delivery people. Maybe I'll give that a go!

Thanks for the tip,

The Messenger

----
==To a [[Nechryael]]==
{{Letter|To a Nechryael

Hey Mr Nechryael, I gotta question for you. Are you in any way related to the Mahjarrat? I've met a couple Mahjarrat in some ancient ruins in the desert and they kinda look similar to you (although I must say you look much more muscular than they did, do you work out?).

Sincerely,

TheWiseLoner}}

Dear TheWiseLoner,

What are you on about? I met a couple of Mahjarrat in the bad old days and they looked absolutely nothing like me! You ought to get your eyes checked. Thanks for the compliment though - we exercise when we can, but it's a bit difficult in this old place. We tried organising a fun run once, but it upset the crawling hands.

Until next time,

Mr Nechryael

----
==To [[My Arm]]==
{{Letter|To My Arm,

How are your farming adventures going? It only felt like yesterday when I was watching you pick your very first Gout Tuber.

Maybe we can go on another adventure together sometime soon?

Sincerely, your strangely-named human friend}}

Hey Friend!

Goutweed growin' very nicely here in Weiss! Lots of tasty tubers. An' that's not only thin' growin' around here! Snowflake an' My Arm 'ave been plantin' some seeds of our own, an' we're proud to announce dat a new friend is on der way! My Arm can already hear the STOMP STOMP of little feet... even though we didn't use no seed dibber!

Hope you come and meet der little one soon. Maybe we name dem after you!

All der best

Your friend

My Arm (an' Snowflake)

----
==To [[Pontak]]==
{{Letter|Dear Pontak,

Fifteen years ago, on the 29th of Septober in the 168th Year of the Fifth Age, I wrote you to give an update in my quest for Zamorak's teddy bear, Saradomin's wig, a left-handed chisel, cheese from the moon, and a dodo egg.

First, I'd like to apologize for my language; I was but a mere child at the time. In the many years passed, I've since completed the trials once over again, and even slain the mighty Jormungand, and am now known as Thorkar Dräpare. It's safe to say I have grown substantially over these years. To that end, I'd like to make amends and extend my hand for a truce. What say you?

Secondly, I wanted to give you an update. I've since located the Mage Gower's skull; you'll be interested to know that he actually still possesses it. I pen this note from inside my sleeping bag, which I use often. I had Guthix's climbing boots, but sold them many years ago after their street price skyrocketed. And, recently, I traveled to Zanaris and was able to craft a delicious cheese from the many cows that inhabit that realm. So, I have now retrieved that item as well. However, despite my many efforts, I have yet to locate the dodo egg. However, rest assured: my quest continues to this day.

I hope this finds you well, and I do sincerely wish you all the best.

aragornjack1}}

Ha! Hello, Thorkar, formerly known as Thorlor.

I remember your letter well! It was this one, wasn't it?

{{Letter|Dear Pontak,

Why do you hate all outlanders? You are mean. And by the way, I bought Zamoraks Teddy Bear, but i got rid of it. It tried to attack me. You wouldnt want one of those. And I have the left handed chisel. All regular chisels are left handed. And Saradomin's wig belongs to Veleornia. She's actually a boy who is bald. She went to the makeover mage, and he forgot to give her hair. Oh and one more thing, Im level 57 and im soooo much stronger than you. I only need to kill Koschei the Deathless and then Ill have seven votes and Brundt will let me in. hahahahah u are a noob.

Hope you have a bad life,

aragornjack1}}

Good to see your spelling's improved, at least. We Fremenniks learn how to use apostrophes before we can talk! So you've completed multiple trials, have you? Slain the Jormungand? Humph. Still not so impressive by Fremennik standards, but I suppose I can forgive you your earlier outburst. I remember how I reacted when Old Chief Svinulf told me I had to build a longboat with nothing but a glass hammer and a box of assorted knots! It took me at least a week. Good old Svinulf - now there was a man who knew the real meaning of the word 'trial'!

Maybe I'm out of touch? No, this new generation is just soft. Pah! Even Askeladden's Pet Rock could fetch me a measly Dodo Egg.

Still, I will say you've made good progress with the rest of the list. In another 15 years, maybe you'll finish it off - and my left toenail will be chieftain!

Keep looking,

Pontak

----
==To the [[Bank of Gielinor]]==
{{Letter|To the representative of the Gielinor Banking system,

What was your reaction the first time you saw someone try to deposit the mythical Godsword? Are there items that the wonderful Banking staff prefer or resent? My second question is about your new branch being opened in the near future. What was the process like acquiring the land rights in the newly discovered Ancient wing of the God Wars Dungeon? I’ve been enormously impressed by your commitment to customer service (like your work with the chest on Ironman Isle on Fossil Island), and I’m very impressed that you’re taking this to the next level. Will you be getting KC for your personnel every time that items need to be brought down?

Gratefully yours, The Adventurer}}

Good day, Hablapata!

Frankly, being handed a Godsword was quite a shock! Especially since there were three more in the queue. It's not every day you have to stick an item thought to be the stuff of myth and legend in the vault - well, actually, it is. It's every day. Hardly anything surprises us Bankers, although we're never thrilled to have to handle 28 Buckets of Compost. Can't complain, though. At least it's in a bucket!

Obviously I can't share the full details, but it's all thanks to a mysterious tip-off. A messenger just showed up one day and said we might like to expand to the Ancient Prison. We didn't even know such a place existed! But as you've observed, we're always looking to improve customer service, so we made the necessary preparations and hey presto - there's your Bank.

Unfortunately we won't be getting KC for trekking down there. We'd hardly be the most popular Bank in Gielinor if our staff went around murdering people!

Thank you for your enquiry,

B. Anker, Official Representative of the Bank of Gielinor

----
==To [[Skotizo]]==
{{Letter|To Skotizo,

Your feet so big, but flipper so small, why?

Sincerely, a flipper enthusiast}}

To the doomed Wasting EXP:

These Dark Claws of mine are indeed awe-inspiring. I can only assume that whichever lowly wretch thou hire to turn them into 'flippers' has to shrink them to fit thine puny human tootsies. Embarrassing!

Yours mockingly,

Skotizo

----
==To [[Konar quo Maten]]==
{{Letter|To Konar quo Maten,

I found a Brimstone Key and it says it's for your heart. Can the next task you give me be a nice walk in the park with you?}}

Bringer of Death,

Unfortunately a walk in the park (even a nice one) would not serve the needs of balance. Perhaps you'd like to slay some Steel Dragons in the Brimhaven Dungeon instead?

Yours,

Konar quo Maten

x

----
==To [[Mambo-duna-roona]] and [[Patrick]]==
{{Letter|Dear Mambo-duna-roona and Patrick,

I recently built a [[Large Orrery]] in my home, and after studying it I am perplexed. It shows our home planet Gielinor, alongside our moon Zanaris, in orbit around a star. However, I also noticed a second planet with two moons also orbiting our star.

What is this planet? Is it inhabited? Are its moons similarly inhabited by magical fairies like Zanaris? I'd love to know.

With great inquisitiveness,

Worldstream}}

Dear Worldstream,

How wonderful to see an adventurer like yourself with such a passionate interest in astronomy! That Orrery looks to be based on our model here at the Observatory.

Unfortunately, Scorpius' notes on the project were lost in one of the many goblin raids, although we can guess that the model does indeed show our own planet, and one other. However, I must stress that this is all conjecture. I myself have not observed these other celestial bodies, and judging by this model they'd be completely uninhabitable. Take the large planet in the middle, for example; if Scorpius is to be believed, half of it would never even see daylight! What sort of creatures could survive in such conditions?

Perhaps these fairies of yours could manage it? Ha - fairies on the moon. What a charming idea. Take my advice, young astronomer - lay off Patrick's wine!

Yours,

Professor Groningen

----
==To [[Bob the Cat]]==
{{Letter|Can you please tell Bob the Cat I said pspspspsps?}}

''Oh, Freak_Mage... I'm sure he knows.''

----

That's all from Postie Pete for now! There will be a new Reddit thread soon where you can submit letters for the next Gazette, so keep your eyes out for that!

{{Postbag from the Hedge}}

content:
{{Transcript|item}}

Our exploration of the caves is complete, and has been a success.

Our lord's followers have dwindled in number, it is true. Few of us who shared his exile from Kourend are still alive to serve him today.

Many fell to the perils of the cave; they were weak, and our lord teaches us that the weak should expect no other fate.

Others forced our lord to discipline them, some for outright treachery, some for other failings. Let them remain in this cave as a testament to the supremacy of our lord!

Our lord has graciously appointed me as his new High Priest, and I shall endeavour to be a more worthy servant than my vain predecessor.

Nevertheless, though our party was reduced in numbers, our lord has led us to victory over the Guardian in the Deep, and has seized the power that he sought.

Now we make our camp in the Guardian's chamber, among the skulls of its former prey. Although I doubt it has been permanently killed, the Guardian will not trouble anyone again for a long time.

The weapons and armour that we have developed in the caves can stay here, in this place of safety. As our lord now wields power over the crystals of the cave, he intends to create a secure seal around our store. He says it would take an earthquake to shatter it!

I am truly awestruck by the power that our lord now wields. If we were to return to Kourend, as he originally planned, I have no doubt that we would regain our former dominion over the kingdom with very little effort.

However, while our lord remains as secretive as ever - in fact, he has become more so after the treachery of our former followers - I sense he has a new plan in mind.

Perhaps the throne of Kourend has become too small a trophy to satisfy the ambitions of Lord Xeric.

title: Transcript:Death on the Isle
content:
{{Transcript|quest}}
{{Transcript list|Patzi|Adala|Wandering Guard|Villa Guard|Head Butler|Constantinius|Cozyac|Pavo|Xocotla|Hutza|Stradius|Costumer|Naiatli|Clodius}}

==Starting the quest==
* '''Patzi:''' Good day! I don't suppose I could trouble you for the briefest of moments?
* {{tcond|If the player does not meet the quest requirements:}}
** '''Player:''' I suppose I could consider being troubled for a little...
** '''Patzi:''' Ah, on second thoughts, you may not be cut out for this job.
** {{tbox|You do not meet all of the requirements to start the Death on the Isle quest.}}
** {{tact|end}}
* {{tcond|If the player meets the quest requirements:}}
** '''Player:''' Good day to you! I could consider being troubled, for the right reasons.
** '''Patzi:''' How does access to a rather fancy party sound as a motivator?
** '''Player:''' Well, just as long as I get to actually enjo-
** '''Patzi:''' I'm sure I can also rustle up some payment to encourange you, if you have any reservations.
** '''Patzi:''' You may even find some... exciting opportunities inside, given the presence of some of Aldarin's wealthiest citizens!
** '''Player:''' So if you're going to this party, would you also be one of Aldarin's wealthiest citizens?
** '''Patzi:''' Alas, I am, quite unfortunately, not rich in money. What I do possess is a certain wealth...
** '''Patzi:''' ... of talent! For you see I am... an actor! Patzi the Grand, they'll call me... eventually.
** '''Player:''' They call me [player name]... just [player name]. So if you're not rich in money, how am I going to get paid, assuming I agree to help you with... whatever it is you want.
** '''Patzi:''' Cutting words, but you need not worry. While you won't be getting paid upfront, I have a feeling that if all goes well, I will soon find myself with more than enough wealth to handsomely reward you.
** '''Patzi:''' And besides, if nothing else, I'm sure you'll have a wonderful time at the party!
** {{tselect|Start the Death on the Isle quest?}}
** {{topt|Yes.}}
*** '''Player:''' I suppose I could do with letting my hair down a little. Alright, I'm in.
*** '''Patzi:''' Wonderful!
*** '''Player:''' So whose party are we going to?
*** '''Patzi:''' Well, that's complicated...
*** '''Player:''' You don't know?
*** '''Patzi:''' Sometimes a man has to follow his heart... and a second hand invitation saying there's a party at Villa Lucens tonight.
*** '''Player:''' Villa Lucens?
*** '''Patzi:''' Yes! The villa is home to an almighty patron of the arts! He even has his own theatre atop the cliffs behind the villa! In fact, the whole reason for this party is because he's showing his new play!
*** '''Player:''' And yet you don't actually know who he is?
*** '''Patzi:''' This opportunity came about quite suddenly. As such, I'm unfortunately not as prepared as I otherwise would be. However, an actor like myself can't turn down the chance to meet with a man like him.
*** '''Adala:''' Not to mention the chance to enjoy a good party.
*** '''Patzi:''' Well said, Adala. Oh that reminds me, [player name], this is Adala. She's also helping me out today!
*** '''Player:''' If you have her, why do you need me?
*** '''Patzi:''' She advertised herself as a bag carrier, so she's here to move my bag around. There's a lot of costumes and props that I travel with, so it's nice to have someone else carry them.
*** '''Adala:''' I'm not going to say no to going to a fancy party, even as the help.
*** '''Patzi:''' As for your part in all this, [player name], with this being a fancy party and all, I'm going to need a butler to help me fit in.
*** '''Player:''' A butler?
*** '''Patzi:''' You know, serving me wine and tending to my needs. Fancy suit and all?
*** '''Player:''' Right... So I don't actually get to enjoy the party at all, do I?
*** '''Patzi:''' Oh I'm sure you will. You'll just have to act a little here and there!
*** '''Player:''' I see... You mentioned a fancy suit. You wouldn't happen to have a butler outfit in that bag you mentioned?
*** '''Patzi:''' I don't believe I do. I don't really take roles like that these days.
*** '''Player:''' Well, in that case, any idea where I might get one, preferably free of charge?
*** '''Adala:''' Lots of the villas around here will have butlers, and butlers mean uniforms.
*** '''Player:''' Are you suggesting I steal one?
*** '''Adala:''' I suppose you could always put it back once you're done.
*** '''Player:''' And I'm sure whoever I take it from will be overjoyed to have had someone else wearing their uniform.
*** '''Patzi:''' Hmm... Maybe I should add a butler's uniform to my vast array of costumes after all.
*** '''Adala:''' I doubt they'll ever even realise. Anyway, I remember seeing some uniforms through a window on the way over here. They were in a villa to the north.
*** '''Player:''' Right... I guess I'm off to find a uniform then.
*** '''Patzi:''' Good luck!
*** {{tact|end}}
** {{topt|No.}}
*** '''Player:''' I'm not really a party person these days, I'm afraid.
*** '''Patzi:''' Quite unfortunate. In that case, please make sure to keep an eye out for me at your local theatre. I'll be a star soon!
*** {{tact|end}}

===Talking to Patzi after rejecting the quest===
* '''Patzi:''' Hello again! Are you feeling more in the partying spirit now?
* {{tselect|Start the Death on the Isle quest?}}
* {{topt|Yes.}}
** {{tact|above}}
* {{topt|No.}}
** {{tact|above}}

==Getting a uniform==
===Talking to Patzi without a uniform===

* '''Constantinius:''' That's not a problem. You can easily keep everyone in the theatre. The only place they'd be able to run to from there is straight off the cliff!
* '''Hutza:''' Constantinius...
* '''Constantinius:''' It's settled then! We will proceed with the play! While we do that, if the killer is still at large, the ever capable [player name] here will ensure they are dealt with!
* '''Player:''' Fine, let's get going then.
* '''Constantinius:''' Oh, no, you can't come with us. I don't want your investigation disrupting things. You'll need to stay out of sight. Why don't you take the back way?
* '''Player:''' The back way?
* '''Constantinius:''' Yes! It's not been used in a while, so it's a little bit precarious these days, but I'm sure you'll manage.
* '''Player:''' Fine. Where do I find this back way?
* '''Hutza:''' The pathway leads around the cliffs to the south. We'll see you at the theatre, [player name].
* {{tbox|The others depart for the theatre.}}
* {{tact|end}}

===Talking to costumer===
* '''Player:''' Hello there.
* '''Costumer:''' Nilsal. Are you the one who's trying to find Livius' killer?
* '''Player:''' That's right. So I'm guessing down here is your domain?
* '''Costumer:''' If you think I have any actual control in here, you'd be sorely mistaken. I don't think anyone could keep these actors in line. They're a... dramatic bunch.
* '''Player:''' Speaking of which, where are they?
* '''Costumer:''' The play will be starting as we speak. They'll all be up in the theatre.
* '''Player:''' Right, well in that case, I'd better get to it. I'd like to have a look around down here. Hopefully I can find some sort of clue as to how Livius died.
* '''Costumer:''' Go ahead.
* '''Player:''' I'd also like to ask you a few questions, if that's okay?
* '''Costumer:''' Of course.
* {{tselect|Select an option}}
* {{topt|What can you tell me about the actors?}}
** '''Player:''' What can you tell me about the actors?
** '''Costumer:''' There's four of them in total... Well... was four I should say.
** '''Costumer:''' There's Naiatli. She was Livius' understudy. After what happened, she's now taking the lead role tonight.
** '''Costumer:''' Then you have Clodius. He's getting close to retirement now so prefers to take on small, but impactful roles.
** '''Costumer:''' Finally there's Quintilia. She's quite new, so she mostly takes on the non-speaking parts.
** '''Player:''' And all of them were in here earlier?
** '''Costumer:''' That's right. Livius went out for his pre-performance drink, as he likes to do. The others all stayed here until after the murder happened.
** '''Player:''' And you're sure none of them could have slipped out at any point?
** '''Costumer:''' I don't think so. I suppose I do get quite engrossed in my work sometimes, so it's not impossible. But I'm sure I'd have spotted someone going up the stairs...
** {{tact|other}}
* {{topt|cond=If the player has searched the crate of poison:|What's the crate of poison for?}}
** '''Player:''' What's the crate of poison for?
** '''Costumer:''' Ah, that was a gift from Constantinius. We were having a bit of a rat problem, so he gave us the poison to deal with them.
** {{tact|other}}
* {{topt|cond=If the player has searched the costume rack:|It seems one of the costumes has a stain on it.}}
** '''Player:''' It seems one of the costumes has a stain on it.
** '''Costumer:''' A stain?
** '''Player:''' Yes, a wine stain. Apparently the costume belongs to Naiatli. Is there any reason the costume would be stained?
** '''Costumer:''' No, none of her characters have any interaction with wine...
** '''Player:''' Do you have any wine backstage?
** '''Costumer:''' Well, the actors do often like to have a drink after a play, but I always ask that they do that outside so as to not risk any damage to the costumes.
** '''Player:''' Interesting...
** {{tact|other}}
*  {{topt|cond=If the player has searched the bookshelf:|Did you know there was a hidden passage in here?}}
** '''Player:''' Did you know there was a hidden passage in here?
** '''Costumer:''' A passage? I had no idea, but I suppose it's not too suprising.
** '''Player:''' How come?
** '''Costumer:''' This is an old villa. Apparently it once played a role in some smuggling operations a long time ago. I could see them having a few secrets to help them with that.
** {{tact|other}}
* {{topt|I'm going to get looking around.}}
** '''Player:''' I'm going to keep looking around.
** {{tact|end}}

===Talking to costumer again===
* {{tselect|Select an option}}
* {{topt|What can you tell me about the actors?}}
** {{tact|above}}
* {{topt|cond=If the player has searched the crate of poison:|What's the crate of poison for?}}
** {{tact|above}}
* {{topt|cond=If the player has searched the costume rack:|It seems one of the costumes has a stain on it.}}
** {{tact|above}}
* {{topt|cond=If the player has searched the bookshelf:|Did you know there was a hidden passage in here?}}

===Searching the costume rack===

===Talking to Hutza or Stradius after investigating the backstage===
* '''Hutza:''' The play is well underway and for all we know there's still a killer out there. I hope you have something for us, [player name].
* '''Player:''' I think I might. It turns out there's a secret passage from the backstage area into the wine cellar. Someone could have got in and out without anyone else knowing.
* '''Player:''' Not only that, but the backstage area has had a rat problem recently. They have plenty of poison for dealing with them. That same poison could easily have been used to kill Livius.
* '''Stradius:''' Great work, [player name].
* '''Hutza:''' But did you find anything that could tell us who did it?
* '''Stradius:''' Yes, we need to confront the killer! Who was it, [player name]?
* {{tselect|Who killed Livius?}}
* {{topt|Patzi.}}
** '''Player:''' Patzi.
** '''Stradius:''' But how? We established that he couldn't have accessed the cellar.
** '''Hutza:''' That's right. The secret passage doesn't change that either as he never left the villa.
** '''Player:''' Okay, not him then.
** {{tact|initial}}
* {{topt|Adala.}}
** '''Player:''' Adala.
** '''Stradius:''' So it was her? But why?
** '''Hutza:''' Adala may be a criminal, but she had no reason to want Livius dead. I don't think it was her.
** '''Player:''' Hmm... Good point.
** {{tact|initial}}
* {{topt|Constantinius.}}
** '''Player:''' Constantinius.
** '''Stradius:''' How would he have gained from killing Livius?
** '''Hutza:''' Exactly. If he's wanted to stop sponsoring him, he could have just done that. No killing needed.
** '''Player:''' I guess you're right.
** {{tact|initial}}
* {{topt|Cozyac.}}
** '''Player:''' Cozyac.
** '''Hutza:''' Because of the debt? That could be a motive, but he never had the means.
** '''Player:''' Hmm... I suppose you're right.
** {{tact|initial}}
* {{topt|More options...}}
** {{tselect|Who killed Livius?}}
** {{topt|Xocotla.}}
*** '''Player:''' Xocotla.
*** '''Hutza:''' She did lie about knowing him, but we never determined any proper motive.
*** '''Stradius:''' I don't think she ever had the opportunity either.
*** '''Player:''' I think you're right actually. Ignore me.
*** {{tact|initial}}
** {{topt|Pavo.}}
*** '''Player:''' Pavo.
*** '''Stradius:''' I thought we'd ruled them out?
*** '''Hutza:''' Do you have new information that changes that, [player name]?
*** '''Player:''' Er... No.
*** '''Hutza:''' Well then it's probably not them.
*** {{tact|initial}}
** {{topt|Naiatli.}}
*** '''Player:''' Naiatli.
*** '''Hutza:''' The understudy that's on stage right now? Why?
*** '''Player:''' As a fellow actor, she had access to the secret passage into the wine cellar where Livius was having his pre- performance drink.
*** '''Hutza:''' But how did she kill him?
*** '''Player:''' The rat poison. Enough of that would easily kill a man. She poisoned his drink so that she could be back out of the cellar before he died.
*** '''Stradius:''' I suppose that makes sense, but she wasn't the only one who had access to that passage.
*** '''Player:''' But she was the only one who had wine on her clothes. Wine isn't allowed backstage, so it must have come from the cellar.
*** '''Hutza:''' Oh, very good! But what about motive?
*** '''Player:''' Constantinius mentioned earlier that she had been in Livius' shadow for some time. Killing him has finally allowed her to take on a leading role.
*** '''Stradius:''' I suppose this does all make sense, but are you certain?
*** '''Player:''' I'd say eighty, maybe ninety percent sure.
*** '''Hutza:''' Well I suppose that will have to be enough. You've not taken us down too many wrong paths today...
*** '''Stradius:''' Except for the whole fake butler act.
*** '''Hutza:''' True, but you were honest about that pretty quickly. We'll wait until the play is over and then we'll take her in.
*** '''Player:''' Wait? But should we not be acting now?
*** '''Hutza:''' Constantinius would kill us if we stopped the performance.
*** '''Stradius:''' And then we'd have another murder mystery on our hands...
*** '''Player:''' Well then we'll have to just speed things along a bit. I'm going out there!
*** {{tact|Player is transported to the stage.}}
** {{topt|Clodius.}}
*** '''Player:''' Clodius.
*** '''Hutza:''' The actor? But why would he do that?
*** '''Player:''' Well, he was one of the few who had access to the secret passage into the wine cellar. He also had access to the rat poison.
*** '''Stradius:''' But what was his motive?
*** '''Player:''' Er... I don't know.
*** '''Hutza:''' We're going to need more than that, [player name].
*** {{tact|initial}}
** {{topt|More options...}}
*** {{tselect|Who killed Livius?}}
*** {{topt|Quintilia.}}
**** '''Player:''' Quintilia.
**** '''Hutza:''' The actress? But why?
**** '''Player:''' She had access to both the secret passage into the wine cellar and to the rat poison.
**** '''Stradius:''' But she doesn't have a motive... She also isn't the only one who had access to the passage and poison.
**** '''Player:''' Ah... Good point.
**** {{tact|initial}}
*** {{topt|The Costumer.}}
**** '''Player:''' The Costumer.
**** '''Stradius:''' Really?
**** '''Player:''' Well, she had access to the secret passage. She claimed not to know about it, but she did know about the history of the villa. She also had access to the rat poison.
**** '''Hutza:''' But why would she kill him? What's the motive?
**** '''Player:''' I... don't know.
**** '''Hutza:''' Sounds like she might not be our killer then, [player name].
**** {{tact|initial}}
*** {{topt|Livius.}}
**** '''Player:''' Livius.
**** '''Stradius:''' You think Livius killed himself?
**** '''Player:''' Well it's the last thing anyone would expect.
**** '''Hutza:''' It's the last thing anyone would expect because it obviously didn't happen! Let's try considering some more plausible candidates.
**** {{tact|initial}}
*** {{topt|You two.}}
**** '''Player:''' You two.
**** '''Stradius:''' Us? But surely we'd remember...
**** '''Hutza:''' Of course it wasn't us! Stop messing around, [player name]!
**** {{tact|initial}}
*** {{topt|More options...}}
**** {{tselect|Who killed Livius?}}
**** {{topt|Me.}}
***** '''Player:''' Me.
***** '''Stradius:''' You?! Goodness, it's the crime of the century! Right, come with us!
***** '''Player:''' Wait! I was joking!
***** '''Hutza:''' Stop playing around, [player name]! We have a killer to deal with!
***** {{tact|initial}}
**** {{topt|The dog.}}
***** '''Player:''' The dog.
***** '''Hutza:''' The dog? But how would a dog do something like this?
***** '''Stradius:''' Never underestimate a dog, Hutza.
***** '''Hutza:''' Okay, but even if the dog did have the means, it didn't have the opportunity, not to mention motive...
***** '''Player:''' Okay, fine, not the dog.
***** {{tact|initial}}
**** {{topt|I don't know yet. I need to review the evidence.}}
***** '''Player:''' I don't know yet. I need to review the evidence.
***** '''Hutza:''' Be quick, [player name].
***** {{tact|end}}
**** {{topt|Previous options...}}
***** {{tact|initial}}

===Talking to Hutza or Stradius again===
* '''Stradius:''' We need to confront the killer! Who was it, [player name]?
* {{tact|above}}

==The Stage==
===Talking to Hutza===
* '''Hutza:''' Did you want to leave?
* {{tselect|Select an option}}

* {{topt|No.}}

* {{qact|Player is transported to the stage.}}

===Attempting to go through the guest entryway===
* '''Villa Guard:''' Shouldn't you be on stage?

===Talking to Naiatli===
* '''Naiatli:''' At last, the vile villain shows themselves!
* '''Player:''' Villain? The only villain here is you, murderer!
* '''Naiatli:''' I am no murderer! What vexatious allegations you come at me with!
* '''Cozyac:''' I'm not sure about this new character. Are they even in costume?
* '''Player:''' Do not pretend you don't know! Your lies are at an end!
* '''Constantinius:''' I don't think this was in the original script...
* '''Naiatli:''' I've overcome so much! I won't fall at this last hurdle!
* '''Player:''' Lay down your arms! Your heroic deeds are fabrications!
* '''Naiatli:''' Never! Now swing at me!
* {{tact|Player attacks Naiatli, resulting in her taking three damage.}}
* '''Naiatli:''' Argh! You're stronger than I thought... I need to regroup!
* {{tact|Naiatli runs back.}}
* {{tact|end}}

===Talking to Naiatli again===
* '''Player:''' Face me!
* '''Naiatli:''' Ha! You've stepped into my trap.
* '''Player:''' A trap?
* '''Clodius:''' {{overhead|Aha, villain! This is where you fall!}}

===Attacking Clodius===
* {{tact|Player attacks Clodius, resulting in him taking five damage.}}
* '''Player:''' {{overhead|You're no match for me!}}
* '''Clodius:''' {{overhead|I'm sorry... You'll have to fight alone.}}

===Attacking Naiatli===
* '''Naiatli:''' How could you be this powerful?
* '''Player:''' It's all part of my grand plan. I grow stronger with every passing moment!
* {{tact|Player attacks Naiatli, resulting in her taking eight damage.}}
* '''Naiatli:''' I can't keep up with this!
* '''Player:''' Then flee again, ignoble hero!
* {{tact|Naiatli runs back.}}
* {{tact|end}}

===Attacking Naiatli again===
* '''Naiatli:''' I must make my last stand... Could you find it in your heart to stay your hand?
* '''Player:''' And let you live to foil my plans another day? I'm afraid that's not the game we play!
* {{tact|Player attacks Naiatli, resulting in her taking four damage. Naiatli falls on the stage.}}
* '''Naiatli:''' And so I take my leave from this mortal coil!
* '''Constantinius:''' Bravo!
* '''Pavo:''' Well that was a twist, wasn't it?
* '''Player:''' Naiatli, I know you killed Livius. Why?
* '''Naiatli:''' I've been stuck in the shadow of that man for too long. He wouldn't even let me fill another role...
* '''Player:''' Murder is a bit far though. Could you not have just... lightly poisoned him?
* '''Naiatli:''' You don't understand... I never poisoned him... I just tripped him. All I wanted was to put him out of action. A small injury would've been enough for him to not perform this evening...
* '''Player:''' What happened?
* '''Naiatli:''' He'd had so much to drink. He fell harder than expected, and he wouldn't get up... I fled... I never wanted him to...
* '''Player:''' Oh, Naiatli... Come on, let's get you to the guards.
* {{tact|Player is transported inside the villa.}}
* '''Player:''' Stradius, Hutza, it's been a surprising pleasure working with you to solve this case.
* '''Stradius:''' I can't believe it was all an accident...
* '''Hutza:''' [player name], you've done well. I'd like to apologise for our hasty arrest earlier. Your commitment to helping us has been commendable.
* '''Stradius:''' To be fair to us, you did seem like the perfect suspect.
* '''Player:''' I suppose I did, but no harm done. I'm just glad we got it all sorted out, though I don't think Patzi is going to be paying me any time soon...
* '''Hutza:''' You win some and you lose some I guess. All the best, [player name]!
* {{tact|end}}

==Post-quest dialogue==
===Talking to Hutza===
* '''Hutza:''' You were quite impressive up on stage. Maybe you should take up a career in acting... or investigating crime.
* {{tact|end}}

===Talking to Stradius===
* '''Stradius:''' Thanks for your help again, [player name]. It's good to know people like you are around.
* {{tact|end}}

===Talking to Patzi===
* '''Player:''' Still here, Patzi?
* '''Patzi:''' No thanks to you! This was meant to be a big moment for me, and you totally upstaged me!
* '''Player:''' Are you angry at me for getting involved in all of this? Did you forget that it was you that hired me?
* '''Patzi:''' I hired you to make me look better!
* '''Player:''' And I don't think I did too bad a job. You never got kicked out, even though you did bring a thief in with you.
* '''Patzi:''' I suppose.
* '''Player:''' So how about that payment you promised?
* '''Patzi:''' Ah... Well... You see...
* '''Player:''' Yes, I thought as much.
* {{tact|end}}

===Talking to Constantinius===
* '''Constantinius:''' Well, I never imagined you'd be quite the actor!
* '''Player:''' I have to admit, I rather surprised myself there.
* '''Constantinius:''' I don't suppose you'd like to be acting here in the future? To be honest, I'd prefer you to that odd fellow that brought you to my door.
* '''Player:''' It's a kind offer, but I'm afraid it was a one-time job.
* '''Constantinius:''' A shame to be sure.
* '''Constantinius:''' Anyway, do feel free to wander around the villa whenever you fancy. I don't recommend drinking from the wine fountain though.
* {{tact|end}}

===Talking to the costumer===
* '''Costumer:''' You were very brave for going on stage to confront a killer. Looks like you did well to get her to surrender without damaging her costume.
* '''Player:''' It was very well made. Makes the job of not damaging it much easier!
* '''Costumer:''' Why thank you! I credit my needles for the good work.
* '''Player:''' Would I be able to get one of them for my own purposes?
* '''Costumer:''' I suppose I could part with one... If you're careful not to lose it.
* '''Player:''' I'll be careful.
* {{tbox|pic=Costume needle detail.png|The costumer gives you one of her special needles.}}
* {{tact|end}}

===Talking to the Head Butler===
* '''Head Butler:''' After all that, are you sure I can't convince you to join the union?
* '''Player:''' Actually, I was wondering if...
* '''Head Butler:''' Kuani! I'll need to run and grab my forms, but if you wait there just a moment...
* '''Player:''' I was going to ask if you had any spare equipment...
* '''Head Butler:''' Spare equipment?
* '''Player:''' I may have a need to mask my identity again in the future... or perhaps carry a tray around.
* '''Head Butler:''' You're certain you don't want to join the union as well?
* '''Player:''' I'm sure.
* '''Head Butler:''' I see. In that case, which equipment would you like?
* {{tselect|Select an option}}
* {{topt|The ram mask.}}

* {{topt|The bird mask.}}
