title: Transcript:Slayer task tips
content:
{{Transcript}}

==Slayer monsters==
{| class="wikitable align-center-2" style="width:700px;"
! style="width:30%;" | Monster
! Tip text
|-
|[[Aberrant spectres]]
|Aberrant Spectres are fetid, vile ghosts. The very smell of them will paralyse and harm you. A nosepeg will help ignore their stink.
|-
|[[Abyssal demon]]
|Abyssal Demons are nasty creatures to fight. They aren't really part of this realm, and are able to move very quickly to trap their prey.
|-
|[[Aquanite]]s
|Aquanites rely on their lures for both offensive and defensive purposes. Whilst their hides are resistant to slashing attacks, a well timed cut is capable of severing the lure.
|-
|[[Araxytes]]
|Try not to die.
|-
|[[Banshees]]
|Banshees use a piercing scream to shock their enemies, you'll need some Earmuffs to protect yourself from them.
|-
|[[Basilisks]]
|Basilisks, like Cockatrice, have a gaze which will paralyse and harm their prey. You'll need a Mirror Shield to protect you.
|-
|[[Bloodveld]]
|Bloodveld are strange demonic creatures, their long rasping tongue has magical properties so it pierces straight through physical defences.
|-
|[[Brine rats]]
|Brine Rats can be found in caves that are near the sea. They are hairless, bad-tempered and generally unfriendly.
|-
|[[Brutal black dragon]]
|Brutal Black Dragons can be found in the Kourend Catacombs. They are more vicious than regular Black Dragons and use melee, magic and dragonfire attacks.
|-
|[[Cave bugs]]
|Cave Bugs are like Cave Crawlers, except smaller and easier to squish, though they still have a fondness for plants.
|-
|[[Cave crawlers]]
|Cave Crawlers are small and fast, often hiding in ambush. Avoid their barbed tongue or you'll get poisoned.
|-
|[[Cave horror]]s
|Cave Horrors can be found under Mos Le'Harmless. You will need a Witchwood Icon to fight them effectively.
|-
|[[Cave kraken]]
|Cave Kraken are found in subterranean lakes north of Eagles' Peak. They're very hard to damage with ranged or melee attacks, so try Magic.
|-
|[[Cave slime]]
|Cave Slimes are the lesser cousins of Jellies. Don't be fooled though, they can still be dangerous as they're often poisonous.
|-
|[[Cockatrice]]
|Cockatrice, like Basilisks, have a gaze which will paralyse and harm their prey. You'll need a Mirror Shield to protect you.
|-
|[[Crawling hands]]
|Crawling Hands are undead severed hands, fast and dexterous they claw their victims.
|-
|[[Custodian stalker]]
|Custodian Stalkers are capable of a dangerous bleed magic, so be ready to hold your ground against them.
|-
|[[Dark beasts]]
|Dark Beasts are large, dog-like predators. Their massively muscled bodies protect them from crushing weapons.
|-
|[[Drake]]s
|Drakes are only found in the depths of the Karuulm Slayer Dungeon. You'll want some Boots of Stone to protect yourself from the heat, and an anti-dragon shield if you're not quick on your feet.
|-
|[[Dust devils]]
|Dust Devils use clouds of dust, sand, ash, and whatever else they can inhale to blind and disorientate their victims. Make sure to wear a facemask when fighting them.
|-
|[[Fever spiders]]
|Fever Spiders are giant spiders that carry the deadly Spider Fever. If you don't want to catch it I suggest you wear Slayer Gloves to fight them.
|-
|[[Fossil Island wyvern]]
|Fossil Island Wyverns are extremely dangerous in different ways. To stand a good chance of surviving you'll need some elemental shielding from their icy breath.
|-
|[[Gargoyles]]
|Gargoyles are winged creatures of stone. You'll need to fight them to near death before breaking them apart with a Rock Hammer.
|-
|[[Gryphon]]s
|Gryphons are native to the Great Conch. They are known for killing their prey by throwing or dropping them, so it would be wise to make sure you're too heavy to be picked up.
|-
|[[Harpie bug swarms]]
|Harpie Bug Swarms are pesky critters that are hard to hit. You need a lit bug lantern to distract them with its hypnotic light.
|-
|[[Hydra]]s
|Hydras are only found in the depths of the Karuulm Slayer Dungeon, you'll want some Boots of Stone to protect yourself from the heat. They spit poison and have access to melee, ranged and magic attacks.
|-
|[[Infernal Mage]]s
|Infernal Mages are dangerous spell users, beware of their magic spells and go properly prepared.
|-
|[[Jellies]]
|Jellies are nasty cube-like gelatinous creatures which absorb everything they come across into themselves. Their magical acids bypass physical defences.
|-
|[[Killerwatts]]
|Killerwatts store huge amounts of energy in their bodies, which is released if they are touched. You'll need to wear heavily insulated boots to counter this shocking effect.
|-
|[[Kurask]]
|Kurask are large brutal creatures with very thick hides. You'll need a Leaf-Tipped Spear, Sword or Battle-axe, Broad Arrows, or a Magic Dart to harm it.
|-
|[[Lesser nagua]]
|Nagua are creatures well versed in magic. Their reckless fighting style leaves them open to melee attacks.
|-
|[[Lizard]]s
|Lizards are large reptiles with tough skin. Those found in the desert will need you to douse them with freezing water to finish them off after a tough battle. You'll need boots of stone to protect your feet for those at Mount Karuulm.
|-
|[[Mogres]]
|Mogres are a type of aquatic Ogre that is often mistaken for a giant mudskipper. You have to force them out of the water with a fishing explosive.
|-
|[[Molanisks]]
|Molanisks are subterranean creatures. You can find them in caves deep below the ground. I heard that the goblins have recently had trouble with some, but they use a bell of some sort to deal with them.
|-
|[[Mutated zygomites]]
|Mutated Zygomites are hard to destroy. They regenerate quickly so you will need to finish them with fungicide.
|-
|[[Nechryael]]
|Nechryael are demons of decay which summon small winged beings to help them fight their victims. Their minions can bypass protective prayers so be sure to wear thick armour.
|-
|[[Pyrefiends]]
|Pyrefiends are beings of fire and molten rock, they're quick and agile but weak to water spells.
|-
|[[Rockslugs]]
|Rockslugs are strange stoney slugs. You'll need to fight them to near death before finishing them off with Salt.
|-
|[[Sea snakes]]
|Sea Snakes are long and slithery with a venomous bite. The larger ones are more poisonous, so keep an eye on your health.
|-
|[[Skeletal wyverns]]
|Skeletal Wyverns are extremely dangerous and they are hard to hit with arrows as they slip right through. To stand a good chance of surviving you'll need some elemental shielding from its icy breath.
|-
|[[Smoke devil]]
|Smoke Devils emit a lot of noxious gases & are slow and lumbering. You'll need a facemask in order to get anywhere near them.
|-
|[[Sourhogs]]
|Sourhogs have highly acidic saliva and are known to spit when provoked. You should ensure that you wear a pair of Reinforced Goggles to protect yourself.
|-
|[[Spiritual creatures]]
|Spiritual Creatures can be found in the icy caverns near Trollheim, supporting the cause of their chosen god. Wearing equipment aligned with each of the gods can help you avoid undesired conflict.
|-
|[[Terror dogs]]
|Terror Dogs are the personal pets of Tarn Razorlor. Wherever you find him, you will find them. They are bad-tempered and generally unfriendly.
|-
|[[Turoth]]
|Turoth are large vicious creatures with thick hides. You'll need a Leaf-Tipped Spear, Sword or Battle-axe, Broad Arrows, or a Magic Dart to harm them.
|-
|[[Venator]]s
|Venators are bloodthirsty creatures found exclusively in Vampyrium. These creatures can only be slain by weapons suited to defeating vampyres.
|-
|[[Wall beasts]]
|Wall Beasts are really much larger creatures but you'll only see their arms. You'll want something sharp on your head to stop them grabbing you.
|-
|[[Slayer task/Warped creature|Warped creatures]]
|Warped Creatures can supposedly be found within a mysterious dungeon on the eastern edge of the Poison Waste. Be aware that to defeat them, you'll need to purify them in some way.
|-
|[[Wyrm]]s
|Wyrms are draconic creatures that come in a few different varieties. You'll find the regular kind in the Karuulm Slayer Dungeon, while their deadlier cousins, the strykewyrms, can be found in the Charred Dungeon. Both varieties exist on Wyrmscraig.
|}

==Regular monsters==
{| class="wikitable align-center-2" style="width:700px;"
! style="width:30%;" | Monster
! Tip text
|-
|[[Adamant dragon]]
|Adamant dragons can fire metal bolts which sap your health, for a chunk of their own. Watch out for their poison bombs too.
|-
|[[Ankou]]
|Ankou are undead skeletal ghosts. Their blows can be powerful but they have limited defences, so killing them quickly is often the best way to protect yourself.
|-
|[[Aviansie]]
|Aviansies{{sic|the plural of aviansie is aviansie}} are bird-like creatures found in the icy dungeons of the north. Melee weapons can't reach them, so use Magic or Ranged attacks.
|-
|[[Bandit (disambiguation)|Bandits]]
|Bandits band together for protection against enemies such as yourself.
|-
|[[Bats]]
|Bats are rarely found on the ground, so you'll have to fight them while they're airborne, which won't be easy with melee.
|-
|[[Bears]]
|Bears are tough creatures and fierce fighters, watch out for their powerful claws.
|-
|[[Birds]]
|Birds aren't the most intelligent of creatures, but watch out for their sharp stabbing beaks.
|-
|[[Black demon]]
|Powerful weapons known as demonbane weapons can be used to quickly defeat even powerful demons like the Black Demon with greater ease.
|-
|[[Black dragon]]
|Black Dragons are the strongest dragons and very fierce, watch out for their fiery breath. Those with higher slayer knowledge and who seek a much tougher, but substantially more rewarding foe, may wish to fight Brutal versions of these creatures in the Kourend Catacombs.
|-
|[[Black Knight]]
|Black Knights like using black armour and weapons, this makes them susceptible to magic attacks.
|-
|[[Blue dragon]]
|Like all dragons, Blue Dragons have thick scales and a powerful fiery breath. Stabbing weapons and heavy bolts are best suited to piercing their defences.
|-
|[[Bronze dragon]]
|Bronze Dragons are the weakest of the metallic dragons, their bronze scales are far thicker than normal bronze armour.
|-
|[[Catablepon]]
|Catablepon are mythical, cow like, magical creatures. Beware their weakening glare.
|-
|[[Chaos druid]]
|Chaos Druids are druids who've turned to evil. Some of them have spells that can harm you, or even teleport you back to them if you flee.
|-
|[[Cows]]
|Cows are bigger than you, so they'll often hit fairly hard but are usually fairly slow to react.
|-
|[[Crabs]]
|Crabs can be found all across Gielinor. They don't hit very hard but they can take a while to kill.
|-
|[[Crocodile]]
|Crocodiles are large reptiles which live near water. You'll want to have a stabbing weapon handy for puncturing their thick scaly hides.
|-
|[[Dagannoth]]
|Dagannoth are large sea dwelling creatures which are very aggressive. You'll often find them in caves near sea water.
|-
|[[Dark warrior]]
|Dark Warriors wear protective armour. If you want to fight them with melee, try crush-based attacks. Or try magic instead.
|-
|[[Dogs]]
|Dogs are much like Wolves, they are pack creatures which will hunt in groups.
|-
|[[Dwarves]]
|Dwarves are a small but tough race of miners, often using pickaxes to pierce their opponents armour.
|-
|[[Earth warrior]]s
|Earth Warriors are a kind of earth elemental, grind them to dust with blunt weapons.
|-
|[[Elves]]
|Elves are quick, agile, and vicious fighters which often favour bows and polearms.
|-
|[[Ent]]s
|Ents are walking tree-people. Bring a hatchet to chop their wood once you've slain them.
|-
|[[Fire giant]]
|Like other giants, Fire Giants have little to no magical ability, and they're particularly weak to water spells.
|-
|[[Flesh crawler]]
|Fleshcrawlers are scavengers and will eat you - and anyone else, given the chance.
|-
|[[Frost dragon]]s
|Frost dragons reside beneath the island of Grimstone. They have thick scales and powerful icy breath. Dragonfire protection is a must.
|-
|[[Ghosts]]
|Ghosts are undead so magic is your best bet against them, even more so if you use wind spells.
|-
|[[Ghoul]]
|Ghouls aren't undead but they are stronger and tougher than they look. However they're also very cowardly and will run if they're losing a fight.
|-
|[[Goblin]]s
|Goblins are mostly just annoying, but they can be vicious. Watch out for the spears they sometimes carry.
|-
|[[Gorak]]s
|Goraks are extremely aggressive creatures. They have been imprisoned on an alternative plane, which is only accesible by using the fairyrings. Be extremely careful, their touch drains health as well as skills!
|-
|[[Greater demon]]
|Demons are particularly weak to water spells. Though Greater Demons are not the strongest type of demon they are still dangerous.
|-
|[[Green dragon]]
|Like all dragons, Green Dragons have thick scales and a powerful fiery breath. Unless you can stay out of their reach, bringing dragonfire protection is a must.
|-
|[[Hellhound]]
|Hellhounds are a cross between Dogs and Demons. They are dangerous with a fierce bite, but have all of the same weaknesses as most demons.
|-
|[[Hill giant]]
|Hill Giants often wield large weapons, learn to recognise what kind of weapon it is and act accordingly.
|-
|[[Hobgoblin]]
|Hobgoblins carrying spears are often trained warriors. If you want less of a challenge, fight the ones that are unarmed.
|-
|[[Ice giant]]s
|Like other giants, Ice Giants have little to no magical ability, and they're particularly weak to fire spells.
|-
|[[Ice warrior]]s
|Ice Warriors are a kind of ice elemental, shatter them with blunt weapons or melt them with fire.
|-
|[[Icefiend]]s
|Icefiends are beings of ice and freezing rock, they're quick and agile but weak to fire spells.
|-
|[[Iron dragon]]s
|Iron Dragons are some of the weaker metallic dragons, their iron scales are far thicker than normal iron armour.
|-
|[[Jungle horror]]
|Jungle Horrors can be found all over Mos Le'Harmless. They are strong and aggressive, so watch out!
|-
|[[Kalphites]]
|Kalphites are large insects which live in great hives under the desert sands. Their chitin is weak to crushing weapons and the larger varieties can be poisonous.
|-
|[[Lava dragon]]
|Lava dragons live in a volcanic area of the Wilderness. Their bones are considered highly worthy offerings by the gods.
|-
|[[Lesser demon]]
|Demons are weak to magical attacks. Though Lesser Demons are relatively weak they are still dangerous.
|-
|[[Lizardmen]]
|Lizardmen have a poisonous bite. Their shamans have many peculiar tricks - make sure they don't jump on your head.
|-
|[[Magic axe]]s
|Magic Axes have a mind of their own. You may find magic or slash-based melee attacks are slightly more effective against them.
|-
|[[Mammoth]]s
|Mammoths plod around the Wilderness. They're big and not very smart, so you can probably trap them on the terrain and kill them from afar.
|-
|[[Metal dragon]]s
|There's lots of different metal dragons from bronze to rune, with the latter being more deadly than the former. Don't forget about their dragon breath!
|-
|[[Scabarites]]
|Scabarites are insectoid creatures, found beyond the Kharidian deserts. Make sure not to fall into one of their pitfall traps or you'll be quickly overwhelmed.
|-
|[[Minotaurs]]
|Minotaurs are large manlike creatures but you'll want to be careful of their horns.
|-
|[[Mithril dragon]]
|Mithril dragons are more vulnerable to magic and to stab-based melee attacks than to anything else.
|-
|[[Monkeys]]
|Monkeys are tricky creatures, they are agile and fairly fast. Learn to anticipate their movements.
|-
|[[Moss giant]]
|Like other giants, Moss Giants have little to no magical ability, and they're particularly weak to fire spells.
|-
|[[Ogre]]
|Ogres are brutal creatures, favouring large blunt maces and clubs, they often attack without warning.
|-
|[[Otherworldly being]]
|Otherworldly Beings are ethereal beings making them weak to magical attack.
|-
|[[Pirate]]s
|Pirates can be found near the sea. They like to collect coins among other things.
|-
|[[Rats]]
|Rats are your everyday pest, but they can get fairly big. Watch out for their sharp piercing teeth.
|-
|[[Red dragon]]
|Red Dragons are very powerful, stronger than most dragons, watch out for their fiery breath.
|-
|[[Revenant]]s
|Revenants can be found in the Wilderness, residing in the deepest cavern of the Forinthry dungeon. They use all three styles of combat, but a charged Revenant bracelet will protect you from their attacks.
|-
|[[Rogue]]s
|Rogues are found in lawless areas, such as the deep Wilderness. They can be very protective of their loot.
|-
|[[Rune dragon]]
|Rune dragons can drain your health to heal themselves. They have some shocking attacks too; avoid those if you can, or wear protective footwear.
|-
|[[Sand Crab]]s
|Sand Crabs can be found on the beaches in Southern Hosidius disguised as piles of sand. They don't hit very hard but they can take a while to kill. If you are up to an even greater challenge, you can face the King Sand Crabs in the Kourend Catacombs.
|-
|[[Scabarites]]
|Scabarites are insectoid creatures, found beyond the Kharidian deserts. They can be extremely dangerous.
|-
|[[Scorpion]]s
|Scorpions are almost always poisonous, their hard carapace makes them resistant to crushing and stabbing attacks.
|-
|[[Shade (disambiguation)|Shade]]s
|Shades are undead so magic is your best bet against them. You can find Shades at Mort'ton.
|-
|[[Shadow warrior]]
|Shadow Warriors are dark and mysterious. They wear spectral plate armour, so crush weapons and magic will give them trouble.
|-
|[[Skeletons]]
|Skeletons are undead so magic is your best bet against them, there is even a spell specially for fighting the undead.
|-
|[[Spiders]]
|Spiders are often poisonous, and many varieties are camouflaged too.
|-
|[[Steel dragon]]
|Steel Dragons are dangerous metallic dragons, their steel scales are far thicker than normal steel armour.
|-
|[[Suqah]]
|Suqahs can only be found on the mystical Lunar Isle. They are capable of melee and magic attacks and often drop hide, teeth and herbs!
|-
|[[Troll]]
|Trolls regenerate damage quickly and have some level of magical defences, but this is easily bypassed by their weakness to fire.
|-
|[[Tzhaar]]
|Tzhaar reside in their cave under the Karamja volcano. Beware as they can call to their fellows for aid.
|-
|[[Undead Druid]]s
|Undead Druids are found within the Forthos Dungeon below the Forthos Ruin in western Hosidius. They attack with both melee and powerful magic attacks.
|-
|[[Vampyre]]s
|Vampyres are extremely powerful beings. An underground group known as the Myreque have been searching for tools to defeat them, which they may be willing to share if you can find them.
|-
|[[Waterfiend]]
|Waterfiends are creatures of water, which live under the Baxtorian Lake. Their watery form is well defended against slashing and piercing weapons, so use something blunt.
|-
|[[Werewolf]]
|Werewolves are feral creatures, they are strong and tough with sharp claws and teeth.
|-
|[[Wolves]]
|Wolves are pack animals, so you'll always find them in groups. Watch out for their bite, it can be nasty.
|-
|[[Zombies]]
|Zombies are undead so magic is your best bet against them, there is even a spell specially for fighting the undead.
|}

==Bosses==
{| class="wikitable align-center-2" style="width:700px;"
! style="width:30%;" | Monster
! Tip text
|-
|[[Abyssal Sire]]
|The Abyssal Sire can teleport you to itself, and can manipulate its environment to attack you.
|-
|[[Alchemical Hydra]]
|The Hydra has many forms. It's poisonous and heavily armoured. Try and weaken it before killing it, somehow.
|-
|[[Araxxor]]
|Araxxor is a very venomous spider, make sure you bring something to protect against it.
|-
|[[Barrows]]
|There are six Barrows brothers with various special attacks. You can kill whichever you like.
|-
|[[Callisto]]
|Callisto roams the Wilderness. His roar can knock you off your feet, and he can hit through prayers.
|-
|[[Cerberus]]
|Cerberus lives in her chamber linked to Taverley dungeon. She attacks with all combat styles so be prepared.
|-
|[[Chaos Elemental]]
|The Chaos Elemental roams the deepest Wilderness. It can teleport you and make you unequip items randomly.
|-
|[[Chaos Fanatic]]
|The Chaos Fanatic has a magic attack that ricochets around, but you can try to dodge it. He can also unequip your items.
|-
|[[Commander Zilyana]]
|Commander Zilyana is in the God Wars Dungeon. She frequently uses magic attacks.
|-
|[[Crazy archaeologist|Crazy]]/[[Deranged archaeologist]]
|You can find Crazy Archaeologists in the Wilderness or on Fossil Island. They throw explosive books that ricochet around, but you can try to dodge them.
|-
|[[Dagannoth Kings]]
|There are three Dagannoth Kings in the cave below Waterbirth Island. You can kill whichever you like.
|-
|[[Duke Sucellus]]
|Duke Sucellus is a demonic horror found in the depths of Ghorrock. You'd be wise to try and weaken him before fighting him head on.
|-
|[[General Graardor]]
|General Graardor is in the God Wars Dungeon. He uses melee and ranged attacks.
|-
|[[Giant Mole]]
|Dig on the mole-hills in Falador Park to enter the mole cave, and bring a lantern he can't extinguish.
|-
|[[Grotesque Guardians]]
|Found upon the top of the Slayer Tower, ring the bell to start the battle, but be careful as the two Grotesques work together.
|-
|[[K'ril Tsutsaroth]]
|K'ril Tsutsaroth is in the God Wars Dungeon. He's poisonous and he can hit through prayers.
|-
|[[Kalphite Queen]]
|The Kalphite Queen is at the bottom of a cave in the desert. Her ranged and magic attacks cannot be blocked by armour.
|-
|[[King Black Dragon]]
|The King Black Dragon's cave is reached by pulling a lever in the Wilderness. An anti-fire shield is strongly recommended.
|-
|[[Kraken]]
|The Cave Kraken boss lives in a cave north of the main cave kraken lakes. It's best fought with magic.
|-
|[[Kree'arra]]
|Kree'arra roosts in the God Wars Dungeon. With the exception of halberds, melee attacks don't work on flying creatures. You'll also need a grappling hook to get in.
|-
|[[The Leviathan]]
|The Leviathan is an ancient sea creature found within the Scar. Its time in the Abyss may have caused it to accrue a weakness to shadow spells.
|-
|[[Maggot King]]
|The Maggot King is found in Vampyrium. It's weak to fire, and the more it burns, the weaker its magical resistance.
|-
|[[Phantom Muspah]]
|Rumour has it that the Phantom Muspah can be found within a dungeon deep beneath Weiss. Whatever it is, it has powerful magic at its disposal, so be prepared.
|-
|[[Sarachnis]]
|Sarachnis can be found in the Forthos Dungeon. She is the mother of the temple spiders, be careful not to get overwhelmed.
|-
|[[Scorpia]]
|Scorpia's minions fill her cave, and will fight to protect their matriarch. Expect to be poisoned.
|-
|[[Shellbane gryphon]]
|The Shellbane Gryphon requires specialised protection. Ensure you are not heavy enough to be picked up, and that you are wearing a Tortugan shield.
|-
|[[Thermonuclear smoke devil]]
|The Thermonuclear Smoke Devil lives in a cave south of Castle Wars. Its attacks hit through prayer. Magical armour is recommended.
|-
|[[TzKal-Zuk]]
|There is no meaningful advice I can give for a challenge of this magnitude. Stay calm and trust yourself, your skills will do the rest.
|-
|[[TzTok-Jad]]
|You'll need to make it through many waves of tough monsters before facing TzTok-Jad, be sure to stock up on supplies.
|-
|[[Vardorvis]]
|Vardorvis is an undead vampyre found within the Stranglewood. He's incredibly nimble, and utilises the environment to his advantage. Be quick to react.
|-
|[[Venenatis]]
|Venenatis lives in the Wilderness. Avoid her sticky webs!
|-
|[[Vet'ion]]
|Vet'ion is in the Wilderness. He dies only when he has been beaten twice. While his dogs guard him, he is immune to damage.
|-
|[[Vorkath]]
|Vorkath can be found on the frozen island of Ungael. You won't last long against him without some form of anti-fire protection.
|-
|[[The Whisperer]]
|The Whisperer is a deadly sirenic nightmare found deep below Ice Mountain. Don't fall for her tricks.
|-
|[[Zulrah]]
|Zulrah is venomous, but if you can learn his behaviour patterns you can avoid a lot of his attacks.
|}

title: Transcript:Slayer's enchantment
Transcript:Sleeping Giants
content:
{{Transcript|Quest}}
{{Transcript list|Kovac}}

==Starting out==
===Entering the cave before starting the quest===
* '''Player:''' I don't think I want to disturb a cave of giants right now...
* {{tact|end}}

===Talking to Kovac===
* '''Hill Giant:''' Wait...
* '''Hill Giant:''' Do not attack!
* '''Player:''' What the... You can talk?!
* '''Hill Giant:''' Do...
* '''Hill Giant:''' do not...
* '''Hill Giant:''' flig... fight.
* '''Player:''' You don't want to fight me?
* '''Hill Giant:''' Want...
* '''Hill Giant:''' no, need...
* '''Hill Giant:''' your help.
* '''Player:''' I must be dreaming. Giants can't talk!
* '''Hill Giant:''' Please...
* {{tselect|Start the Sleeping Giants quest?}}
* {{topt|Yes.}}
** '''Player:''' Okay giant, I'll help you out, but first you need to tell me your name... if you even have one.
** '''Kovac:''' Kovac.
** '''Player:''' Kovac... alright then. My name is [player name]. So, Kovac, what do you need help with?
** '''Kovac:''' Please...
** '''Kovac:''' follow in.
** '''Player:''' Hang on... is this a trick? Are you going to cook and eat me?!
** '''Kovac:''' No...
** '''Kovac:''' follow.
** {{qact|A cutscene plays, showing a workshop too big for regular-sized people to use.}}
** '''Player:''' Woah... What is this place?
** '''Player:''' Did you build this?
** '''Kovac:''' No...
** '''Kovac:''' Kovac...
** '''Kovac:''' accep... ancestor build.
** '''Player:''' Giants built this place?
** '''Kovac:''' Yes...
** '''Kovac:''' long ago.
** '''Player:''' How? Giants don't build, do they? I thought they were brutes...
** '''Kovac:''' Before...
** '''Kovac:''' giants differing.
** '''Kovac:''' Now...
** '''Kovac:''' not.
** '''Player:''' Huh? I don't understand what you mean.
** '''Kovac:''' Look.
** {{tbox|Kovac looks out to the tools around you.}}
** '''Kovac:''' Help fix.
** '''Player:''' You want me to help you by fixing those tools?
** '''Kovac:''' Yes.
** '''Player:''' Okay, I'll help, but first you need to tell me what this place was used for?
** '''Kovac:''' Make...
** '''Kovac:''' wheelpo... weapons.
** '''Player:''' Giants made weapons here?
** '''Player:''' That's incredible! But why do you want to make weapons? Most giants I've come across already have weapons?
** '''Kovac:''' Make...
** '''Kovac:''' giants...
** '''Kovac:''' remember.
** '''Player:''' Remember what?
** '''Kovac:''' Giants...
** '''Kovac:''' not just...
** '''Kovac:''' killers.
** '''Kovac:''' Kovac want...
** '''Kovac:''' help giants remember.
** '''Player:''' I see. To be honest, if I hadn't seen this place myself, I wouldn't have believed you.
** '''Player:''' Alright, Kovac, I'll help you out. What do we need to do first?
** '''Kovac:''' We fix tools...
** {{tact|end}}
* {{topt|No.}}
** '''Player:''' No way! I'm getting out of here. There's no chance I'd trust a giant!
** '''Hill Giant:''' Please...
** '''Hill Giant:''' help.
** {{tact|end}}

==What is this? A workshop for giants?==
===Talking to Kovac===
* '''Player:''' What's left to fix, Kovac?
* '''Kovac:''' Hmm...
* '''Kovac:''' Trip hammer...
* '''Kovac:''' Grindstone...
* '''Kovac:''' Polishing wheel...
* '''Player:''' Thanks!
* {{tact|end}}

===Inspecting objects===
====Big chest====
* '''Player:''' Kovac, where did you get this chest from?
* '''Kovac:''' Hmm...
* '''Kovac:''' ...
* '''Kovac:''' chest store stuff.
* {{tbox|Kovac shrugs...}}
* '''Player:''' Alright then...
* {{tact|end}}

====Crate====
* '''Player:''' What do you keep in this box?
* '''Kovac:''' Hmm...
* '''Kovac:''' stuff.
* '''Player:''' Very insightful...
* {{tact|end}}

====Crucible====
* '''Player:''' What is this, Kovac?
* '''Kovac:''' Hmm...
* '''Kovac:''' look like big bucket.
* '''Player:''' I can see that, but what's it used for?
* '''Kovac:''' Hmm...
* '''Kovac:''' maybe we put things in.
* '''Kovac:''' Kovac need think about it more.
* {{tact|end}}

====Lava pool====
* '''Player:''' Having all this lava here without a barrier is quite dangerous.
* '''Kovac:''' Hmm...
* '''Kovac:''' Kovac agree.
* '''Player:''' Should we try building something to keep us safe?
* '''Kovac:''' Hmm...
* '''Kovac:''' no.
* '''Player:''' Why not?
* '''Kovac:''' Just no swim in the hot juice.
* {{tact|end}}

====Mould jig====
* '''Player:''' What is this table used for, Kovac?
* '''Kovac:''' Hmm...
* '''Kovac:''' look like we put thing on it.
* '''Kovac:''' Kovac not sure what yet.
* '''Kovac:''' Hmm...
* '''Kovac:''' Kovac think about it more.
* {{tact|end}}

====Preform storage====
* '''Player:''' This looks a little dangerous. Quite a perilous place to store something.
* '''Kovac:''' Hmm...
* '''Kovac:''' good place to cook food.
* '''Kovac:''' Hot meat very good.
* {{tact|end}}

====Waterfall====
* '''Player:''' Not everyday you see a waterfall in a cave.
* '''Kovac:''' Kovac drink from waterfall...
* '''Kovac:''' Hydration impote... importent.
* '''Player:''' I agree, it's very important.
* {{tact|end}}

===Reparing the trip hammer===
* '''Player:''' I think this has seen better days. What was it?
* '''Kovac:''' Hmm...
* '''Kovac:''' big hammer.
* '''Player:''' Right... and what did it do?
* '''Kovac:''' Hit things.
* '''Player:''' Very perceptive, Kovac.
* '''Player:''' Let me take a look and see if I can fix it.
* {{tselect|Repair the trip hammer?}}
* {{topt|Yes.}}
** {{tcond|If the player does not have the materials required:}}
*** {{tbox|pic=Oak logs detail.png|pic2=Bronze nails detail.png|You will need an oak log, 5 nails and a hammer to repair the trip hammer.}}
*** {{tact|end}}
** '''Player:''' That looks like it'll do the trick. What do you think?
** '''Kovac:''' Hmm...
** '''Kovac:''' that look right.
** '''Player:''' What's it supposed to do?
** {{tbox|Kovac takes a long look at the trip hammer... }}
** {{tbox|...}}
** '''Kovac:''' Kovac think Kovac figure it out.
** '''Player:''' Go on.
** '''Kovac:''' Trip hammer power by water...
** '''Kovac:''' Water spin wheel and raise hammer.
** '''Kovac:''' Hammer fall and crump sword into shape.
** '''Player:''' That makes sense. Quite resourceful for giants to make something water powered.
** '''Kovac:''' Mhm...
** {{tact|end}}
* {{topt|No.}}
** {{tact|end}}

===Reparing the grindstone===
* '''Player:''' What was this meant to be?
* '''Kovac:''' Hmm...
* '''Kovac:''' Kovac think it was for grinnin... grinding.
* '''Player:''' I see. It looks like it's lost its teeth.
* '''Kovac:''' Kovac conquer.
* '''Player:''' Conquer? It's already broken! Hitting it more won't help.
* '''Kovac:''' Hmm...
* '''Kovac:''' Kovac agree.
* '''Player:''' Right... now we're agreed, I'll see what I can do to fix it.
* {{tselect|Repair the grindstone?}}
* {{topt|Yes.}}
** {{tact|The player begins to fix the grindstone.}}
** '''Player:''' Well that required a bit of elbow grease. It should be good to go now.
** '''Kovac:''' Thank you small one...
** '''Player:''' Didn't want to try and help me?
** '''Kovac:''' Kovac did not know how...
** '''Kovac:''' Kovac beggin... beginning to understand.
** '''Player:''' Can you tell me what this is used for then?
** {{tbox|Kovac takes a long look at the grindstone... }}
** {{tbox|...}}
** '''Kovac:''' Grindstone important...
** '''Kovac:''' We grind sword against stone...
** '''Kovac:''' make sword sharp.
** '''Player:''' So we use it when making swords?
** '''Kovac:''' Yes.
** {{tact|end}}
* {{topt|No.}}
** {{tact|end}}

===Reparing the polishing wheel===
* '''Player:''' Okay, what is this thing? It just looks like a wheel to me.
* '''Kovac:''' Hmm...
* {{tbox|Kovac ponders your question... }}
* {{tbox|...}}
* '''Kovac:''' Kovac think he know.
* '''Player:''' And?
* '''Kovac:''' This polishing wheel...
* '''Kovac:''' make thing shiny.
* '''Player:''' Looks like it's lost its soft edge then.
* {{tselect|Repair the polishing wheel?}}
* {{topt|Yes.}}
** {{tcond|If the player does not have the materials required:}}
*** {{tbox|pic=Wool detail.png|pic2=Oak logs detail.png|You will need some wool, 2 oak logs, 5 nails and a hammer to repair the polishing wheel.}}
*** {{tact|end}}
** '''Player:''' Not my finest work, but I think it will do.
** '''Kovac:''' Hmm...
** '''Kovac:''' Kovac agree.
** '''Player:''' So when would we use the polishing wheel?
** '''Kovac:''' Polishing sword impotan... important.
** '''Kovac:''' Create perfect killing edge...
** '''Kovac:''' very good for sword.
** '''Player:''' That makes sense.
** {{tact|end}}
* {{topt|No.}}
** {{tact|end}}

===Talking to Kovac after all the tools are repaired===
* '''Player:''' That's all the tools repaired. Well... as best as I can do.
* '''Kovac:''' Yes...
* '''Kovac:''' Kovac begin to understand more now.
* '''Player:''' I've noticed your speech has been improving over time as well.
* '''Kovac:''' Kovac know what say...
* '''Kovac:''' but sometime hard say proppel... properly.
* '''Player:''' That's alright, we'll figure it out together.
* '''Kovac:''' Kovac agree. Ready to make sword?
* '''Player:''' Yes! I'm itching to get started.
* '''Kovac:''' Kovac get few things ready first...
* '''Kovac:''' then we can start.
* {{tact|end}}

==Make-A-Sword==
===Talking to Kovac===
* '''Player:''' Okay Kovac, I think I'm ready to make a sword.
* '''Kovac:''' Hmm...
* '''Kovac:''' Kovac feel like things look correct...
* '''Kovac:''' Kovac think you are right.
* '''Player:''' So what do I need to do to make a sword?
* '''Kovac:''' First...
* '''Kovac:''' you will need a coliti... commission.
* '''Player:''' Where can I get one of those?
* '''Kovac:''' Kovac will supply them...
* '''Kovac:''' Kovac already gotten one from old friend.
* '''Player:''' Okay, so what do I need to make?
* '''Kovac:''' Kovac need a {{Colour|#ef1020|Flat Broad}} sword.
* '''Player:''' Great!
* '''Player:''' How do I make that?
* '''Kovac:''' Kovac think we need to fill the...
* '''Kovac:''' how's it called...
* '''Kovac:''' the big stone bucket...
* '''Player:''' Oh, you mean a crucible?
* '''Kovac:''' Yes, thank you...
* '''Kovac:''' Kovac think we need to fill the crucible with metal first.
* '''Kovac:''' Kovac has been connecti... collecting metals...
* '''Kovac:''' They're in that box-crate by entry.
* '''Kovac:''' Use bars and weapons...
* '''Kovac:''' Crucible can take both.
* '''Kovac:''' Load metals into crucible until it looks full.
* '''Kovac:''' While you do that...
* '''Kovac:''' Kovac think about next thing we need to do.
* {{tact|end}}

===Searching crate===
* {{tbox|You rummage through the box... }}
* {{tbox|You find a bunch of metal bars and old weapons!}}
* {{tcond|If the player does not have 20 open inventory spaces:}}
** {{tbox|You will need 20 free inventory slots to take the items from the crate.}}
** {{tact|end}}
* {{tselect|Take the items?}}
* {{topt|Yes.}}
** {{tbox|pic=Bronze battleaxe detail.png|pic2=Iron bar detail.png|You take a selection of bars and weapons from the crate.}}
** {{tact|end}}
* {{topt|No.}}
** {{tact|end}}

===Talking to Kovac after looting the crate===
* '''Player:''' Alright, I've got the metal you said to take from the box. What now?
* '''Kovac:''' You will need to fill the crucible...    
* '''Kovac:''' Add metals, armour or weapon you find to fill it.
* '''Kovac:''' We stick to bronze and iron for this sword...  
* '''Kovac:''' We keep the first sword simple.
* {{tact|end}}

===Talking to Kovac after partially filling the crucible===
* '''Player:''' I've added a few things to the crucible. Is that enough?
* '''Kovac:''' No, we need more...
* '''Kovac:''' 28 metal bars worth. Weapon and armour can go into crucible too but some metal lost when melted down.
* {{tact|end}}

===Talking to Kovac after filling the crucible===
* '''Player:''' Right, that's the crucible full. Can I make the sword yet?
* '''Kovac:''' Kovac think we need to set up a mould.
* '''Player:''' What's a mould used for?
* '''Kovac:''' Hmm...
* '''Kovac:''' Kovac think mould will determine the type of sword to be made.
* '''Kovac:''' Remember, we need a {{Colour|#ef1020|Flat Broad}} sword.
* '''Player:''' Okay, so how do I go about setting up a mould?
* '''Kovac:''' Kovac remember being told a sword is made from three parts...
* '''Kovac:''' a forte, a blade and a tip.
* '''Kovac:''' Use mould jig behind you...
* '''Kovac:''' You can select part for each selecti... section.
* '''Kovac:''' Each mould part is differing...
* '''Kovac:''' They will suit different commissions better...
* '''Kovac:''' Look for parts that match commission.
* '''Player:''' Right... I think I'm with you.
* '''Kovac:''' If you are still confused...
* '''Kovac:''' come back to me.
* {{tact|end}}

===Talking to Kovac before setting the mould===
* '''Player:''' I'm sorry Kovac, but I'm not entirely sure what I'm meant to be doing.
* '''Kovac:''' That is okay...
* '''Kovac:''' Kovac not so sure of himself...
* '''Kovac:''' but you help Kovac, so Kovac help you.
* '''Player:''' Thanks Kovac. You're gentle for a giant.
* '''Player:''' So what was it I needed to do at the mould jig?
* '''Kovac:''' We need to fill each part of the mould...
* '''Kovac:''' Forte, blade and tip.
* '''Kovac:''' We want to use mould parts that match collisi... commission Kovac give you.
* '''Kovac:''' Remember, each part suit a differing sword better...
* '''Kovac:''' Look for ones that match {{Colour|#ef1020|Flat and Broad}}.
* {{tact|end}}

===Talking to Kovac after setting the mould===
* '''Player:''' Right, the mould is setup and the crucible is full to the brim. We must be ready to pour.
* '''Kovac:''' Hmm...
* '''Kovac:''' let me look.
* {{tbox|Kovac takes a look at what you've done... }}
* {{tbox|...}}
* '''Kovac:''' Yes, all things look correct...
* '''Kovac:''' Well done little one. We are ready.
* '''Kovac:''' Pour the metal from the crucible into the mould...
* '''Kovac:''' then take out the preform.
* '''Kovac:''' Once you have done that...
* '''Kovac:''' Kovac will tell how to work the preform.
* {{tact|end}}

===Before picking up the preform===
* '''Player:''' The metal's too hot to pick up!
* '''Kovac:''' Yes.
* '''Player:''' What do I do?
* '''Kovac:''' Cool it down...  
* '''Kovac:''' What do you expect?
* '''Player:''' Ah, of course... How do I do that?
* '''Kovac:''' Kovac do not know. Try pouring water on it.
* {{tact|end}}

===Talk to Kovac after using a bucket of water===
* '''Player:''' I'm not sure what to do next...
* '''Kovac:''' Hmm...

content:
{{Transcript|item}}

===Part 1===
For the attention of all centurions:

Prepare your soldiers for battle, for we set sail at dawn. The target is a Saradominist temple near Hallowvale. The temple has been built underwater, but the Praefectus Classis has devised a plan to move our forces inside. She has acquired the means to teleport large numbers of individuals directly into the temple. While the fleet controls the waters above, your soldiers will be tasked with clearing the temple of all resistance. It is expected that Saradominist resistance will be incredibly high, so prepare accordingly.

===Part 2===
For the attention of all centurions:

The Praefectus Classis has become aware of concerns amongst the soldiers. As we are on final approach, ensure you take the time to make it clear to your legionaries that these concerns have no validity. Our force has been kept light intentionally to ensure we can surprise the Saradominist forces. However, using the same teleportation method she'll use to give us access to the temple, the Praefectus Classis also has the ability to call in any reinforcements we need. Have faith, for our work will ensure the Empire will never fall.

===Part 3===
For the attention of all centurions:

Many of you will never see this, but for those that do, these are your final orders. The battle is lost and we must withdraw. The attempt to call in reinforcements failed, and the temple has been ripped asunder by a rift of unknown power. The rift is growing rapidly and has already claimed much of the fleet. The Praefectus Classis is lost. Retreat is the only option. For those of you that fall, may your sacrifice be forever remembered in the annals of the Eternal Empire.

{{Transcript|item}} ===Raktuber 31st, 166
Dearest Lensa=== Brother Rakkar found this old empty diary on board, I'll fill it with entries of our travels for you to read upon my arrival! ===Pentember 1st, 166
Dearest Lensa=== The storms have been rougher than the seers foretold, we've had to take shelter on Lunar Isle and the Moonclan are not impressed. They say of our voyage west will find nothing but a watery grave, their Kosmos be damned! ===Pentember 23rd, 166
Dearest Lensa=== We've been sailing for weeks now my love and the crew has become weary, supplies run low and Jaldur has no explanation for the lack of fish in these strange waters. Land is on the horizon, hope is not lost. ===Fentuary 5th, 166
Dearest Lensa=== Great news! We've discovered a fishing hamlet in the cold tundra on the coast of this new continent. The locals are quiet... but friendly enough, they've allowed us hospitality providing we help out catching fish. ===Fentuary 12th, 166
Dearest Lensa=== The fish in the waters here are magnificent! We'll have to bring some back for all of you to try, along with the ale! I'm not sure how they're making it but it's strong and makes for great merriment! Jardor found a large snakestone in the recent catch, the locals seem weary of it and demand we take it with us when we leave. ===Septober 17th, 166=== It's been awhile{{sic}} since my last entry, I apologize{{sic}} my dear, but things have taken a turn for the worst. We still remain at the fishing hamlet for brother Barrak and Jardor have a sickness, they mutter words to the snakestone, they claim it whispers back... ===Septober 19th, 166=== Jardor has turned to drinking the ocean, he says it'll bring him closer to the gods... for who he's referring to I do not know. The snakestone lies. ===Septober 21st, 166=== The villagers are gone, something took them in the night, trails lead to an ominous crevasse... I must convince the others that we must flee now, before it's too late. ===Septober 23rd, 166=== It spoke to me, I'm going to stay now. ===Septober 25th, 166=== Rakkar tried to throw the snakestone back into the ocean, Jardor and Barrak made an example of him, he'll be troubling us no more. ===Ire of Phyrrys, ??, ???=== Praise him.
Praise him.
Praise him. Tonight we ascend.

content:
{{Transcript|item}}

I'll show Haris! 'Unworthy' my boot. I'll be swimming in gold and glory when I return with the treasures of the western lands. I heard one of those adventuring lot talk of big-eared lilly-livers, who live behind walls made of diamond. Whatever they're hiding, it's gonna be mine, and if they put up a fight, then they're definitively in for a good hiding. HAH!

Sold the last bit of flax today. No more itchy fields for Blunderguts! Blunderguts is my new pirate name. After all, I'm gonna be a captain of the high seas soon. Maybe I should buy an eye patch, look the part and all that. No one would dare mess with the mighty captain Blunderguts!

Purchased my first vessel from a chap offering a good price, considering the damage. Smells a bit like toast though. He said he swindled it off of one of them lofty hero types. I set sail from Port Sarim tomorrow. Ahoy thar and onwards!

Maybe I should've brought a sextant... How do I find west again? Never eat Toroth{{sic}} slippers... How does it go? Never watch skeletons eat? All this pirating is making me hungry. I've got plenty in the store. Besides, I'm the Captain. So if I want to stop at some tavern along the way I shall... I will hear no more about it.

So I just stopped at this dock, seemed great at first. But no tavern. Some local's directions led me to a giant swamp. Oh Saradomin, the stench of the place, 'Be brave Blunderguts. 'tis what piratin' be all about, forgin' yer own adventure from scratch.' I thought. The locals were friendly enough, 'Come visit our god, you will never starve again' they said. They only tried to feed me to a bloomin' snake! Luckily I must not have looked appetising, bein' so skinny 'n all. With my quick thinking, jumping back into the lady's boat, I made a tactical retreat.

Back to the sea I go. Ahoy thar and onwards!

I saw it. With me unpatched eye, I swear. The walls were mightier than the palace of Varrock. The light caught the tides and it burst into a thousand different colours. But soon as I went to drop anchor, the arrows came. These arrows came at me so fast and so hard I could've swore they was glowin'! I had no choice but to tactically retreat.

Please. If you find this journal, send help. I couldn't save the ship and I'm stranded. All of the people here ignore every word I speak, they're like zombies. Zombies that kill crabs all day long. You can't even eat the crabs, they're almost entirely made of sand!

Ahoy thar, please save me!

* '''Soldier:''' I might as well be if we're going to continue this performance.
* '''Player:''' What do you mean?
* '''Soldier:''' There are no demons coming out of this chasm. If there were, we wouldn't last long.
* {{tselect|Select an option}}
* {{topt|You think the demons would overrun you?}}
** '''Player:''' You think the demons would overrun you?
** '''Soldier:''' Demons don't die the same way we do. We could hold back a few of them, but not an endless stream.
** '''Player:''' You seem to know a lot about them.
** '''Soldier:''' I do, which means I know that guarding the chasm is a pointless endeavour. Not that the lieutenant cares what I think.
** '''Soldier:''' Launching an attack into the chasm would also be pointless. That leaves us with only one other option.
** '''Player:''' Fleeing?
** '''Soldier:''' No. We should talk to them. Try to reach an understanding.
** '''Player:''' Somehow I don't think negotiating with demons will end well.
** '''Soldier:''' If you have a better idea, go ahead.
** {{tact|other}}
* {{topt|Aren't you a bit too calm about this?}}
** '''Player:''' Aren't you a bit too calm about this?
** '''Soldier:''' No. If they wanted to, Yama and his demons could overrun this little squad.
** '''Soldier:''' The fact they haven't means they're probably not interested in doing so. As a matter of fact, they seem quite polite.
** '''Player:''' You've spoken to them?
** '''Soldier:''' I didn't say that, But there's evidence to suggest that Yama and his cult can be reasoned with.
** '''Soldier:''' If Lord Shayzien is interested in diffusing the threat, he should consider trying to reach an agreement with them.
** '''Player:''' I've met Lord Shayzien. He doesn't seem like the type to compromise.
** '''Soldier:''' You've met Lord Shiro Shayzien?
** '''Player:''' Yes, I've met the leaders of all of the houses. Even King Artur Hosidius himself.
** '''Soldier:''' Interesting. You're quite the worldly fellow. Perhaps King Hosidius would make a more level headed negotiator. Maybe you could talk to him?
** '''Player:''' I imagine he's quite busy at the moment.
** {{tact|other}}
* {{topt|Goodbye.}}
** '''Player:''' Goodbye.
** '''Soldier:''' ...
** {{tact|end}}

content:
{{Postbag|issue=21|date=30 July 2007}} {{Transcript list|Wizard Traiborn|Roavar|Aris|Reldo|Jonah who is 7 3/4|Shamus|Tegid|Brian O'Richard|noplayer}} '''There are numbers in my head that I'm quite certain weren't meant for a humble little skull like me! Between Reldo and Gypsy Aris, it's a bit of miracle I managed to even understand Wizard Traiborn. Still, a postie's job is never done, and now I bring you my latest collection of correspondence!''' ---- {{Letter|To the Wizard Traiborn if you please Postie Pete, thanks awfully. He's at the Wizards tower. '''Dear Traiborn.''' How do you do, wot? Tis a nice say for questions, and I happen to have some. The whatsishisface upstairs, I do believe the chap's name is Grayzag, appears to be a master of Whoshewatsits, imps I think, and it jolly well seems to me that he doesn't seem very Sarawhatchamacallit. After all, imps are belonging to whatshisevilface, not very good to have around in a holy spot, wot? Also, I do believe that the jolly old demon has been summoned, please tell me I'm jolly well wrong! Thank you very much, wot!
'''Hylean 1989, a thingygummywhatchamawhatsihisface.'''}} '''Dear Thingygummywhatchamawhatshisface,''' I'm fine, wot wot. Would you like some tea? Oh, it's a letter; no tea then. Whatsisface upstairs? I remember him. Arrived in the middle of the night to become a student, always been very feisty. This was back in the days of Whodoyammacallit, you know, Thingy. Anyway, we were all eating in the dining room. I was eating a nice baked potato with tuna and sweetcorn, my favourite, if I recall. Made it myself with a tuna I'd bought from an adventurer in Draynor-thingymaplace just earlier that day. Said she'd caught it way up in Catherby. I had a holiday there once. It was lovely and sunny. Smelled of fish, though. So where was I? Oh yes: Imps. Great mashed up on toast, too. Tuna that is, not imps. Why would you want to mash up an imp, that's cruel. You do say the strangest things. So, why would thingummybobs be evil? I quite like the wee chaps. Very useful for finding things, like whatdoyamacallits and beads. I found a Nigel coloured one just the other day, never seen one of them before. Darning imp wouldn't let it go, had to blast him out the tower-thingummy first. Was supposed to be mending holes in my thingamagigs with his tiny needle and thread. So, yes. Demon, you say...there's a demon in the Wizard's thingamajig? Where? I went upstair just 5 minutes ago and there wasn't a whatsathingamagiggycalled. There was a very nice chap dressed all in red. I like red. But not beads. Got loads of them. Cupboards full of 'em. Somewhere. Anyway, lit my pipe he did. With his finger. Quite a trick, not sure if I could do that myself. So...who were you again? Why are you in my room? You're trying to steal my caged thingamawhats! Never; away with you. Forgetfully,
'''''Wassmyname, Mageywizardythingamawotsit''''' {{Letter|'''Dear werewolves of Canifis,''' I must first say that werewolves are the best! I would so be one if I could! But anyway... I have studied much of your town and ways of living but one thing has always puzzled me. Why do vampires rule Canifis if there are so many werewolves that could fight against them? In my opinion, werewolves are much better then vampires and I think you could take the vampires and rule Canifis as your own. I would even help! Is there some power that the vampires hold against you? Or do you fear them for some reason? This is one answer that is yet to come to me. Please answer! Werewolves rule! Your fellow werewolf,
'''Magicman4222'''}} '''Magicman4222,''' You don't sound much like a werewolf to me. Why would any werewolf want to rise up against the vampyres? They're great! Ever since I was a pup they've been around, keeping the humans out (except the ones they like to feed on) and us werewolves safe. On top of that, after they have a drink they leave the meat and bones behind for us. It's a good life for the werewolves in Canifis! Sure, we have to give up a bit of blood in a tithe now and then when times are a bit lean for our blood sucking overlords, but that's much better than being hunted to extinction, isn't it? My mammy told me once that werewolves used to live all over the place, but those humans don't like us much (not as much as we like them: mmm, delicious human) so they just started killing us. Now we have to live in Canifis, which is a bit damp but otherwise grand. Hail the vampyres!
'''''Roavar''''' {{Letter|'''Dear Gypsy Aris;''' I recently read that you estimated the Almighty Chaos Elemental's age to be equal to the number of yew trees, minus the number of coal rocks, times the number of werewolves, with an accuracy of plus or minus two thousand. Well, I actually took the time to count up those numbers. And before you go off saying I have too much free time, you're the one who's always pacing back and forth in that little tent of yours, asking for some silver to read someone's fortune, while you're really asking for gold. Anyways...According to my game...er...RuneScape manual, there are 211 coal rocks in RuneScape, since the last revision of the manual. And using the map included with the manual, I counted there to be 34 yew trees in RuneScape. And finally, using my uber teleportation skillz, I went to Canifis to take a census of those werewolves. Where I counted there to be 16, and then recounted there to be 15, and then had to run/escape before I got torn to shreds. Those werewolves don't exactly take kindly to you pointing at them. By now, you've probably fallen asleep but I'll continue anyways. The number of yew trees (34) - the number of coal rocks (211) * the number of werewolves (15) is -2655. Which, give or take 2000, would be -4655 ~ -655. (34 - 211) x 15 = -2655 The Chaos Elemental may be able to alter space, but he/she/it can't alter time, as anyone who has fought him/her/it can tell you. So I ask: You can alter time, as I have seen while trying to kill the Oneiromancer or whatever he was, so why are you unable to estimate the Chaos Elemental's age, even with an error margin of 2000? And no, we all know you don't have a mini-garden of yew trees like the witch near Al Kharid does. I eagerly await your response, > '''Chaos Crater''', who is clearly inferior to the Chaos Elemental.}} Hello Chaos Crater, I knew you'd send me this letter, so I prepared this reply in advance: '''Dear Chaos Crater,''' First things first, it's rather presumptuous to believe that you have seen every coal rock and every yew tree in this absurdly massive world. You may have counted all of the trees and rocks that you have personally seen, but you've failed to take into account that the world is significantly larger than you've seen. Further to that, the Chaos Elemental is, by nature, a being of pure chaos. It's not particularly difficult to assume that his age is equally chaotic. When I provided those details they were correct, but now his age has changed and is equal to the following formula: Number of pies consumed in RuneScape yesterday plus the square root of the area of the Wilderness in acres, divided by the depth of the port at Ardougne in fathoms. Take this number and find the nearest prime. That's how old the Chaos Elemental will be when you receive this letter. And before you say it, I know you can't possibly figure that one out: you adventurers eat far too many pies. You're welcome.
'''''Gypsy Aris''''' {{Letter|'''Hello young childerkin of Karamja!''' You may not remember me but i helped save you from the Gublinch by freezing them with snowballs i made from conviently placed snow difts. A while after the snow had melted and Shanty Claws had left i returned to your home in search of some demons of a lesser kind to kill. On my way to their domain i spot you jmping for joy, free from the Gublinch. I was delighted that you were still safe and free from harm. I must ask you though...as i came back to your home i saw you were still jumping? Don't you three ever get tired? or do the sugars from those sweets keep you going? Thanks for answering
'''Runite Man5'''}} '''‘Ello Roo Nightmans,''' Fanks loads fer savin us mister. Dem gublunches smelt of boiled sweets and wet dogs like nan does. Anyway seems like yer intrested in our jumpin mister so eres why we jump. 1. Jumpin is better than minin. I never wanna go minin ever again cos jumpin is so much more funner. Im gonna be a jumpin pure an only get my jumpin stats up. I’m gonna get a jumpin skillcape wiv a jumpin emote an everyun will want me to do their high level jumpin for em. 2. If you jump enough then yer start forgeting stuff that appened that morning cos yer memmerys start to leap outta yer ears. 3. If you jump fast enuff then you look taller. 4. If yer all jump at once den the world is lighter an thats amazin. Fanks for yer letter.
'''''Jonah who is 7 3/4''''' {{Letter|'''Dear Reldo,''' Over the past 6-8 years of my adventuring (It has become very hard to keep track of the times), I have always wondered a few things. Being, obviously, a pre-middle school dropout, I have not leared some basic things. This can make it quite hard when I have big meetings, and don't know where to go when. For you see, I have never learned much about the calendar on Gielinor. I know a few things though, from books that I have found. Just a few dates, and days, but not much at all. The few months I know of are:
Bennath
Raktuber
Pentember
Septober
I also know that there are at least 32 days in Bennath. What I would like to know from you is:
1. What are the months in our Calendar called? (In order please.)
2. How many days are in each month?
3. How long is a day? (I should know this, but for some reason, whenever I'm awake it's light out.)
4. How many years into the Fifth Age are we?
5. What is todays date? (The date you respond.)
Thank you Reldo,
From the King of Spam,
'''Mistmonk''' (ps, please try to make copies of the great books you must have soon, I would love to read them!) (pss, I know there must be some books in your library that I find interesting, I mean come on!)}} '''Dear Mistmonk,''' Ah, a most excellent letter. I shall answer the easiest of your questions first. Presently, we are in the 169th year of the 5th Age. The length of a day, of course, is equal to one cycle of the sun and the moon. There are ten months in the RuneScape calendar. They are:
Rintra (39 days)
Moevyng (38 days)
Bennath (32 days)
Raktuber (34 days)
Pentember (38 days)
Fentuary (31 days)
Septober (38 days)
Ire of Phyrrys (40 days)
Novtumber (39 days)
Wintumber (36 days)
An extra day is added to Moevyng every four years to account for an anomaly in the way the calendar has been calculated. Moevyng Day, as it is called, tends to fall in the middle of the month. Pentumber, Septober and Novtumber are named as such for being, respectively, the fifth, seventh and ninth months of the year. The most intriguingly-named month is the Ire of Phyrrys. My colleagues over at the Observatory have uncovered the charred remains of a diary that belonged to Phyrrys, apprentice to the astronomer Scorpius. Early entries in Phyrrys's diary tell of how he was attempting to figure out the RuneScape calendar, based upon the astronomical studies his mentor was conducting. However, a few pages have survived of Scorpius's own diary, heavily hinting at Phyrrys's ineptitude, and how at the culmination of the apprentice's initial calendar research, he'd failed to account for a whole forty days. This is backed up in Phyrrys's own diary entries, whereby from this date on, his anger (ire) seemed to grow and grow at his inability to work these forty days into the calendar. It is assumed that a later inhabitant of the Observatory found these notes and, quite easily, corrected the mistake by placing them between Septober and Novtumber, naming the month in honour (or more likely in jest) of the 'challenged' Phyrrys. Regards,
'''''Reldo''''' {{Letter|'''Dear the Itinerent Leprechaun Posse:''' I have conducted an informal poll of several fellow wayfaring adventurers and feel confident enough to express the fervent sentiments of my farming associates. If it were possible to rope you to a stake or tree, I'd be forever ecstatic!! Your incessent wanderlust has often left me befuddled. I look up, you're here, when I look back, you're there! And forbid I should be growing sweetcorns, the greens and yellows comingle, leaving me wondering where you've made off to this time. I run from patch to allotment to tree and though I am physically deft, I wish not to set forth on yet another adventure just to locate or catch up to you when happening upon my next farming chore. Please, limit yourselves!! Until next time, I still claim to '''DunoNuthin.''' PS: Thank you for holding all my tools.}} '''DunoNuthin?''' Is that yer name? What sort’o a name is that? Yer want a good leprechaun name like Nigel. I’ll call you Nigel, lad. So, Nigel, yer be wantin’ to know about me brothers in the tool trade. Well settle down, laddy, and I’ll tell yer a bit about leprechauns. Leprechauns love two things, lad. Gold and nature. We hold yer tools and we help out wi’ your farming because, to be sure, it’s a nice change to see one o’ you elephant-sized folk carin’ about what’s under yer feet. We don’t mind standin’ around with spades stickin’ out of our back pockets in rain or shine but we can’t fight our natural urges no matter how hard we try. When we feel the tingle of a rainbow in the air we have to follow it wi’ all our hearts for at the end of every rainbow there’s a pot of gold to be had. I’ve never found one yet, but there are stories passed down from the ones whose hair has long turned grey. They say the pot of gold at the end of a rainbow is so large yer can do the backstroke in it, so they do. So we’ll hold yer tools lad, but don’t deny us the pot of gold that’s in the mind of every one of us, will ye? '''''Shamus the Leprechaun''''' {{Letter|'''Dear Tegid,''' Dont you ever get sick of washing clothes day in and day out? Every time I pass by you, to go to Taverly Dungeon, your always right there, kneeled down in that same exact spot washing all of you and your friends robes. How come they never take a turn? Your always stuck there with no time to have fun or even explore Taverly Dungeon. You know all work and no play makes Tegid a dull boy! '''Yours sincerely, Guitaristguy.'''}} '''Dear long grey smear,''' Blast you, boy! Your letter incensed me so much that I washed it. Darned if I can remember what it said, so I’ll answer the questions I normally get asked.
1) Kaqemeex, if you left them in your robes then they would have been washed.
2) This is a white wash, Witch. Blood will make everything pink.
3) There were two socks in the basket when I gave it to you. I suppose we have sock gremlins now?
4) No, you can’t borrow my soap. Illuminating, I’m sure. Anyway, a man of the cloth must get back to his duties. '''''Tegid''''' {{Letter|'''Dear Brian O'Richard,''' You may hear this alot, but you look awfully familiar! What with your bald head and stylish clothes. Come to think of it, your name is also familiar. There seems to be some connection between you and someone else but I can't quite put my finger on it. I believe this someone else was the host of a maze and also played the harmonica. I don't suppose you have commited your life to looking like someone else, acting like him and also changing your name similar to his hmm? Don't hesitate to reveal yourself!
'''Archer Page'''}} '''Dear Archer,''' I would like, if I may, to take you on a strange journey... I wasn’t always bald, you know. Once upon a time, I had a fully head of luscious, wavy hair, but it was stripped from me like leaves in a forest fire! It was my friends’ fault... “Eat nutritious high protein and swallow raw eggs,” they said, “Try to build up your shoulders, chest, arms and legs.” It was such an effort, a rigorous plan, but they insisted, “In seven days we will make you a man.” Turns out, the excessive exercise caused me enormous stress, at which point my precious hair started to fall out. They said it was age, but I don’t buy it. Anyway, I’ve got over it now... honestly... THEY DIDN'T LIKE ME! THEY NEVER LIKED ME! ...sorry... erm... Will you start the fans, please! Did I just say that?
'''''Brian O'Richard''''' ----
'''Wise Old Crafts'''
This month I've managed to convince the crafty Baba Yaga to provide a replica of her house for you. It's a bit of a challenge unless you have a Crafting level of 99, though, so pay attention to the instructions! First, [[:File:Postbag from the Hedge - Somethingorotherwotsit (1).jpg|click here]] to see the parts of the model. Once you have a paper version, simply follow the steps below: #Cut out each part. Note that you should cut around them, and not along all of the lines with the exception that dotted lines can be cut as normal. To help you make sense of that, you should note that both F parts are actually two parts each, so you should cut along the dotted lines in the middle. #Score the other lines to make the model easier to fold. Any part with a dot on it will eventually be glued to another, so it's a good idea to keep that mind as you go. #Assemble part A, which is the main part of Baba Yaga's house. #Connect the two halves of the roof, part B. They join together along the long red edge, so the completed roof should rise up at each end. #Attach the roof to the house. Admire your handiwork. #Assemble the steps, part C. These attach just below the door to Baba Yaga's house. #To make the legs, first assemble the two part Ds. Be aware that they should make a wide 'V' shape. #Assemble the feet by constructing both Es and attaching an F to each side (these are the toes on the house's chicken legs). #Attach the feet to the smaller end of the legs, then attach the broader end to the two spotted squares underneath the house. #Resist the urge to squeal with delight when you discover that you have now completed Baba Yaga's house! If you've correctly assembled the model, you should have something like this: [[File:Postbag from the Hedge - Somethingorotherwotsit (2).jpg|center]] If you're anything like Postie Pete, though, you'll probably find yourself with the steps glued to your forehead and the legs sticking out of your nostrils (Postie Pete has a Crafting level of 1). '''That's it from me for now, but I'll see you all again next month, so keep sending me your letters and paintings! Send your letters to postbag@jagex.com.''' '''Don’t forget – when you send us your amazing creations we can’t accept links, so please don’t send them to us!''' '''Next month... stuff!''' '''Postie Pete''' {{Postbag from the Hedge}}

content:
{{Transcript|quest}}
{{incomplete|Other NPCs you can talk to for the resistance recruitment section, one-off branched dialogue with Elena, Lord Amlodd and others. Also missing Rebel Scout dialogue}}
{{transcript list|Edmond|Alrena|King Lathas|Knight of Ardougne (NPC)|Elena|Milli Rehnison|Martha Rehnison|Ted Rehnison|Councillor Halgrive|Carla|Jethick|Kilron|Omart|Priest (West Ardougne)|Nurse Sarah|Woman (West Ardougne)|Chadwell|Clerk|Silk merchant|Baker|Silver merchant|Gem merchant|Fur trader (East Ardougne)|Spice seller|Town Crier|Zenesha|Estate agent|Probita|Aemad|Kortan|Priest (East Ardougne)|Doctor Orbon|Bartender (Flying Horse Inn)|Man (Song of the Elves)|Woman (Song of the Elves)|Essyllt|Lord Iorwerth|Iorwerth Warrior|Iorwerth Archer|Arianwyn|Morvran|King Thoros|Ysgawyn|Ilfeen|Eluned|Islwyn|Lord Baxtorian Cadarn{{!}}Baxtorian|Lord Ieuan Amlodd|Lady Tangwen Trahaearn|Memory of Seren|Lord Piquan Crwys|Lady Carys Hefin|Lord Iestin Iorwerth{{!}}Iestin|Mawrth|Iona|Eoin|Lady Kelyn Ithell|Lady Ffion Meilyr|Kamen|Klank|Niloof|Thorgel|General Hining|Rebel Warrior|Rebel Scout|Fragment of Seren}}

==Starting out==
===Talking to Edmond===
* '''Player:''' Hey, how's it going?
* '''Edmond:''' Not good at all my friend. It's Elena, she's been taken...
* '''Player:''' Taken? By who?
* '''Edmond:''' The Knights of Ardougne. They claimed she was inciting rebellion against the king. Apparently she's been going around telling people that the plague isn't real...
* '''Player:''' Oh dear... This is a problem.
* '''Edmond:''' Is there anything you can do to help us? It feels wrong to ask given what you've done for us before, but we're desperate.
* {{tselect|Start the Song of the Elves quest?}}
* {{topt|Yes.}}
** '''Player:''' I'm sure this is all just a misunderstanding. Let me try talking to the king.
** '''Edmond:''' Thank you friend.
** {{tact|end}}
* {{topt|No.}}
** '''Player:''' I can't help I'm afraid.
** {{tact|end}}

===Talking to Alrena===
* '''Alrena:''' Edmond tells me you're helping Elena again. Thank you so much.
* '''Player:''' It's not a problem.
* {{tact|end}}

==Talking to the king==
* '''Player:''' Good day my lord.
* '''King Lathas:''' Hello [player name]. What can I do for you?
* '''Player:''' I'm here to talk about Elena, apparently she's been imprisoned.
* '''King Lathas:''' That she has. She was making some heinous accusations.
* '''Player:''' That the plague is fake?
* '''King Lathas:''' Exactly.
* '''Player:''' Right... But you and I both know that she's right, the plague is fake.
* '''King Lathas:''' That's not the point. As I've explained to you before, the plague is a necessary evil. We can't have her exposing the truth and risking everything.
* '''Player:''' But King Tyras is dead, what exactly are we risking?
* '''King Lathas:''' My brother may be dead but the Dark Lord is still a threat. Until that threat is gone, the plague must remain.
* '''Player:''' So you won't free Elena?
* '''King Lathas:''' No. I can't take any risks. Now I'm afraid I have business to attend to. You should be on your way.
* '''Player:''' I see. I guess I should let her father know.
* {{tact|end}}

===Talking to him again===
* '''Player:''' Good day my lord.
* '''King Lathas:''' Hello [player name]. What can I do for you.
* '''Player:''' About Elena...
* '''King Lathas:''' We've been through this already. I will not have the girl freed. She is a threat to Ardougne and will remain imprisoned.
* '''Player:''' I see. I guess I should let her father know.
* {{tact|end}}

===Talking to the Knight of Ardougne===
====Climbing down the prison stairs without knight armour====
* '''Knight of Ardougne:''' Sorry citizen. Only Knights of Ardougne are allowed in the prison.
* {{tact|end}}

====Talking to Knight without knight armour====
* '''Player:''' Good day.
* '''Knight of Ardougne:''' Hello there citizen. What can I do for you?
* '''Player:''' What's down these stairs?
* '''Knight of Ardougne:''' These stairs lead to the Ardougne Prison. It's home to thieves, murderers and everything in between.
* '''Player:''' Sounds lovely. Can I go in?
* '''Knight of Ardougne:''' I'm afraid not citizen. Only the Knights of Ardougne are allowed into the prison and I can see that you are no knight.
* {{tact|end}}

==Making a knightly disguise==
===Talking to Edmond after completing the disguise===
* '''Edmond:''' Hello there. Have you spoken to the king yet?
* '''Player:''' I have.
* '''Edmond:''' And?
* '''Player:''' He won't be freeing her I'm afraid.
* '''Edmond:''' But why? I know all this plague business has got her a bit emotional, but can't he see that she's just upset?
* '''Player:''' He said she was a threat to Ardougne.
* '''Edmond:''' A threat? But she's no danger to anyone. Why does he think that way?
* '''Player:''' Well the thing is...
* '''Edmond:''' What?
* '''Player:''' Well... She's right. The plague is a lie. That's why the king had her imprisoned. He was afraid she'd expose the truth.
* '''Edmond:''' The plague is a lie? What do you mean the plague is a lie?
* '''Player:''' I guess I have some explaining to do.
* '''Edmond:''' You most certainly do.
* '''Player:''' Well, it all started after I freed Elena from West Ardougne. As you can imagine, she was still keen on helping the plague victims and asked me to help her find a cure.
* '''Player:''' We sent some samples to her old teacher, Guidor in Varrock. He ran some tests and found out that the plague isn't actually real. I confronted the king on this and he admitted it.
* '''Edmond:''' But why?
* '''Player:''' The king told me that his brother, King Tyras, was corrupted by the Dark Lord while exploring the lands to the west.
* '''Player:''' As Tyras was the king of West Ardougne, King Lathas decided to cordon the city off to keep the rest of the world safe.
* '''Player:''' The plague was the excuse he gave for the quarantine.
