title: Transcript:Viggora
content:
{{Transcript|npc}}

==Without a ghostspeak amulet==
* {{tcond|When spoken to without a ghostspeak amulet:}}
* {{trandom}}
* {{topt|Dialogue 1}} 
** '''Player:''' Hello there.
** '''Mysterious ghost:''' Wooo?  Woooo woo woooooo wooooo woooowooo wooo woooooo woo!
** '''Player:''' You don't say?
** '''Mysterious ghost:''' Woo! WOO WOOOOO WOOWOOWOO WOO WOOOOO!
** '''Player:''' You don't say!
** '''Mysterious ghost:''' Wooowoowoooooo.... Woowoowoo? Woooo, wooowoo wooowooowooo!
** '''Player:''' Well, I guess you didn't say.
** {{tact|end}}
* {{topt|Dialogue 2}} 
** '''Player:''' Hello there.
** '''Mysterious ghost:''' Wooo?  Woooo woo woooooo wooooo woooowooo wooo woooooo woo!
** '''Player:''' Yeah, I don't want to brag, but seriously: I am SOOOO rich....
** '''Mysterious ghost:''' Woo! WOO WOOOOO WOOWOOWOO WOO WOOOOO!
** '''Player:''' Yeah, I know they say money doesn't bring you happiness, but sometimes I just like to open my bank account and look at all of the stuff I own and just think to myself:
** '''Player:''' Wow. I am soooooo rich.
** '''Mysterious ghost:''' Wooowoowoooooo.... Woowoowoo? Woooo, wooowoo wooowooowooo!
** '''Player:''' Well, us rich alive people don't want to waste all day spending time with you poor dead people, because I'm just sooooo rich I have to go now, and very possibly make myself even richer.
** '''Player:''' See ya around ghosty!
** {{tact|end}}
* {{topt|Dialogue 3}} 
** '''Player:''' Hello there.
** '''Mysterious ghost:''' Wooo?  Woooo woo woooooo wooooo woooowooo wooo woooooo woo!
** '''Player:''' Yeah, I heard about that, ha-ha-ha!
** '''Mysterious ghost:''' Woo! WOO WOOOOO WOOWOOWOO WOO WOOOOO!
** '''Player:''' With a MACKEREL? Ouch!
** '''Mysterious ghost:''' Wooowoowoooooo.... Woowoowoo? Woooo, wooowoo wooowooowooo!
** '''Player:''' Well, it was fun. Let's do it again sometime.
** {{tact|end}}
* {{topt|Dialogue 4}} 
** '''Player:''' Hello there.
** '''Mysterious ghost:''' Wooo?  Woooo woo woooooo wooooo woooowooo wooo woooooo woo!
** '''Player:''' Why, thank you very much!
** '''Mysterious ghost:''' Woo! WOO WOOOOO WOOWOOWOO WOO WOOOOO!
** '''Player:''' I know, but what are you going to do?
** '''Mysterious ghost:''' Wooowoowoooooo.... Woowoowoo? Woooo, wooowoo wooowooowooo!
** '''Player:''' Well, I guess that's always true in the long run. See you around, weird invisible dead person!
** {{tact|end}}
* {{topt|Dialogue 5}} 
** '''Player:''' Hello there.
** '''Mysterious ghost:''' Wooo?  Woooo woo woooooo wooooo woooowooo wooo woooooo woo!
** '''Player:''' Yeah it's not bad, but I prefer cooked chicken.
** '''Mysterious ghost:''' Woo! WOO WOOOOO WOOWOOWOO WOO WOOOOO!
** '''Player:''' Maybe, but nothing beats a home cooked pie!
** '''Player:''' Man, I love pie!
** '''Mysterious ghost:''' Wooowoowoooooo.... Woowoowoo? Woooo, wooowoo wooowooowooo!
** '''Player:''' You don't say? I never knew that. Well, I must be going, see you around.
** {{tact|end}}
* {{topt|Dialogue 6}} 
** '''Player:''' Hello there.
** '''Mysterious ghost:''' Wooo?  Woooo woo woooooo wooooo woooowooo wooo woooooo woo!
** '''Player:''' We get signal!
** '''Mysterious ghost:''' Woo! WOO WOOOOO WOOWOOWOO WOO WOOOOO!
** '''Player:''' Somebody set up us the bomb!
** '''Mysterious ghost:''' Wooowoowoooooo.... Woowoowoo? Woooo, wooowoo wooowooowooo!
** '''Player:''' You have no chance to survive make your time.
** '''Mysterious ghost:''' Woo?
** '''Player:''' All your base are belong to us.
** {{tact|end}}
* {{topt|Dialogue 7}}
** '''Player:''' Hey, don't think you can talk to me like that!
** '''Mysterious ghost:''' Woo! WOO WOOOOO WOOWOOWOO WOO WOOOOO!
** '''Player:''' Are you threatening me?
** '''Mysterious ghost:''' Wooowoowoooooo.... Woowoowoo? Woooo, wooowoo wooowooowooo!
** '''Player:''' Just because you're already dead, doesn't mean I can't find a way to hurt you ghosty!
** {{tact|end}}
* {{topt|Dialogue 8}}
** '''Player:''' No, I've never been there in my life and CERTAINLY didn't steal anything when I was!
** '''Mysterious ghost:''' Woo! WOO WOOOOO WOOWOOWOO WOO WOOOOO!
** '''Player:''' Are you calling me a liar?!?! I have never stolen a thing in my life, and I resent the implication that I am the kind of morally depraved individual that would steal someone else's hard earned
** '''Player:''' money from their very pockets!
** '''Player:''' Or cakes. Or fur. Repeatedly. For long periods at a time.
** '''Mysterious ghost:''' Wooowoowoooooo.... Woowoowoo? Woooo, wooowoo wooowooowooo!
** '''Player:''' Well if you are going to take that attitude, then I have nothing further to say on the matter, and bid you good day!
** {{tact|end}}

==After [[Curse of the Empty Lord]]==
* '''Player:''' Hello.
* '''Mysterious ghost:''' Hello yourself.
* {{tselect|Select an Option}}
* {{topt|Talk about Viggora's story.}}
** '''Player:''' I really liked your little story. Can you tell me another one?
** '''Player:''' Preferably something with a big fight and lots of explosions!
** '''Mysterious ghost:''' ...You are a very strange young [man/woman].
** {{tact|end}}
* {{topt|Ask for more ghostly robes.}}
** '''Player:''' Could I have more of those ghostly robes you gave me?
** '''Mysterious ghost:''' It seems as though the curse that keeps me here extends to my very clothing... which piece do you want?
** {{tact|opens2=Ghostly robes reclaim interface}}
** {{tact|receives=the requested piece(s) of [[ghostly robes]]}}
** '''Mysterious ghost:''' Here you go.
** {{tact|end}}

==Speaking to the wrong Viggora==
* {{tcond|When spoken to in a location not in the player's [[Curse of the Empty Lord]] sequence:}}
* {{trandom}}
* {{topt|Dialogue 1}} 
** '''Player:''' Hello there.
** '''Mysterious ghost:''' The endless tragedy of fate... Why must you torment me so?
** '''Player:''' Alright, alright, calm down, calm down. All I said was 'hello'!
** {{tact|end}}
* {{topt|Dialogue 3}} 
** '''Player:''' Hello there.
** '''Mysterious ghost:''' You can see me?
** '''Player:''' Uh... yes?
** '''Mysterious ghost:''' And you understand my words?
** '''Player:''' Well, most of them...
** '''Mysterious ghost:''' This is incredible! How can such a thing have come to pass?
** '''Player:''' What can I say? I'm a professional.
** {{tact|end}}
* {{topt|Dialogue 4}} 
** '''Player:''' Hello there.
** '''Mysterious ghost:''' Hello back at you.
** '''Player:''' So what's a nice ghost like you doing in a place like this?
** '''Mysterious ghost:''' I suppose you think that's funny?
** '''Player:''' Well... Mildly amusing I guess.
** '''Mysterious ghost:''' I don't think I want to talk to you anymore.
** {{tact|end}}
* {{topt|Dialogue 5}} 
** '''Player:''' Hello there.
** '''Mysterious ghost:''' Hello stranger. It is rare indeed that I meet one who can see my presence, let alone one who can understand my words.
** '''Player:''' Soooo.... Is it fun being a ghost?
** '''Mysterious ghost:''' Does it look like fun to you?
** '''Player:''' Erm... Well, yes actually.
** '''Mysterious ghost:''' Then you are a fool, and I will waste no more words upon you.
** '''Player:''' What, not even 'goodbye'?
** '''Mysterious ghost:'''  
** '''Player:''' Sheesh, what a grouch. You'd think you'd have more of a sense of humour being dead and all.
** {{tact|end}}
* {{topt|Dialogue 6}} 
** '''Player:''' Hello there.
** '''Mysterious ghost:''' Mortal... Take heed of my example, and waste not your life, lest you may suffer the same fate as myself...
** '''Player:''' Huh? You mean someone did this to you?
** '''Mysterious ghost:''' You have ascertained the truth in my words...
** '''Player:''' So who did it to you? And why?
** '''Mysterious ghost:''' Events of moons past, I remember not clearly...
** '''Player:''' Fine help you are then.
** {{tact|end}}
* {{topt|Dialogue 7}} 
** '''Player:''' Hello there.
** '''Mysterious ghost:''' Hello stranger.
** '''Player:''' So.... Invisible ghost haunting the same place for thousands of years, huh?
** '''Mysterious ghost:''' You have no idea...
** '''Player:''' Well, bad luck and all that. See ya around!
** {{tact|end}}
* {{topt|Dialogue 8}} 
** '''Player:''' Hello there.
** '''Mysterious ghost:''' Hello.
** '''Player:''' So you're a ghost, huh?
** '''Mysterious ghost:''' Apparently.
** '''Player:''' In which case I only have one thing to say to you:
** '''Mysterious ghost:''' ...what?
** '''Player:''' Guess you don't have the amulet of humanspeak, huh?
** '''Mysterious ghost:''' ...huh?
** '''Player:''' Yeah, that's right. WOO! WOOOWOOO WOO WOOOOWOO! Got no comeback for that, have you?
** '''Mysterious ghost:''' You are very strange...
** {{tact|end}}

* '''Mysterious ghost:''' Hey, I have something for you but you don't have any space for it!
* {{tact|end}}
====With inventory space====
* '''Mysterious ghost:''' Here you go.

* {{tact|end}}

* '''Wandering impling:''' Oh yes. This one here - she is calm and boring. She stays here all the time. She doesn't like to move, but her sister is fidgety and refuses to stay in the same place for more than half an hour.
* '''Player:''' So where is the, errr, fidgety sister at the moment?
* '''Wandering impling:''' Oh she's asleep at the moment. I'm sure she'll go somewhere in the next half an hour though.
* {{tact|end}}

==(Leagues only) If the sister portal is in a locked region==
===Talking to the impling===
* '''Wandering impling:''' I cannot show you this gate's sister on this world.
* {{tact|end}}

===Using "Check-gates" interaction===
* {{mes|Your teleport is blocked as you haven't unlocked access to the {{color|#ff0000|[region name]}} area.}}

title: Transcript:Wanna go stargazing?
content:
{{Transcript}}

[[File:Wanna go stargazing (1).jpg]]

Hi [player name]

Shoot for the Stars!

Is it a bird? Is it a plane? No, it's a new activity!

Shooting Stars was first released in 2008 - but thanks to your votes, it's coming to Old School.

In this activity, you'll hunt down shooting stars with your state-of-the-art Player Owned House telescope, then mine them for star-studded rewards, including Mining XP and brand new items that are unique to the Old School version of Shooting Stars.

Rewards

When you crack open a fallen star, you'll get Mining XP, Stardust! Trade your Stardust with Dusuri for rewards that are truly out of this world.

[[File:Wanna go stargazing (2).jpg]]

Keep your eyes on the skies

You can find Shooting Stars using the telescope in your Player Owned House. Get a rough idea of their location, grab your pickaxe, and head out into the world of Gielinor to mine your well-earned rewards.

title: Transcript:Wanted!
content:
{{External|rs}}
{{Transcript|quest}}
{{Incomplete|Dialogue for accepting to become a squire and making the commorb instead of buying it both need to be reverified. Does dialogue change if going to the Mage of Zamorak first?}}
{{Transcript list|Sir Tiffy Cashien|Sir Amik Varze|Savant|Solus Dellagar|Lord Daquarius|Mage of Zamorak|Woman (Wanted!)|Black Knight (Wanted!)}}

==Starting off==
* '''Sir Tiffy Cashien:''' What ho, [sirrah/milady]. Jolly good show on the old training grounds thingy, what?
* {{topt|Do you have any jobs for me yet?}}
** '''Player:''' Do you have any jobs for me yet?
** '''Sir Tiffy Cashien:''' Well old [boy/gal/bean], looking at the old dossier we have on you here there seems to be a tiny problem, what?
** '''Player:''' Problem? What problem? Er...  and you have a dossier on me???
** '''Sir Tiffy Cashien:''' Well OF COURSE we have a dossier on you! We have a dossier on EVERYONE! It's our job, dontchaknow!
** '''Player:''' Um... okay... So what's the problem?
** '''Sir Tiffy Cashien:''' Well now, seems we made a tiny blunder when we first contacted you to join the Temple Knights, what?
** '''Sir Tiffy Cashien:''' Entirely our own fault, could have been avoided and all that, but bit of a show-stopper, what?
** '''Player:''' What is?
** '''Sir Tiffy Cashien:''' Well old [boy/gal/bean], here's the thing; Only members of the White Knights may join the Temple Knights. By ancient decree, dontchaknow.
** '''Player:''' What? But I am a member of the White Knights! I went and did that stuff with the cabbage and the potion!
** '''Player:''' And I've already done your stupid little mind test thing! You can't get rid of me that easily!
** '''Sir Tiffy Cashien:''' Calm yourself down old [boy/gal/bean]... We have no intention of 'getting rid of you', we are very keen on seeing you join us...
** '''Player:''' Then what's the problem?
** '''Sir Tiffy Cashien:''' Well, it's like this: Although you have performed a mission on behalf of the White Knights, you were never actually working for them.
** '''Sir Tiffy Cashien:''' As I say, when our order was founded, we were expected to take the best of the best, and it was assumed that anyone worth having on the team would have been a White Knight already, what?
** '''Sir Tiffy Cashien:''' Sadly, this is not the case anymore, and the fact that you have to serve as a Squire to a White Knight for a minimum period of five years before you can actually become one tends to put the more short-attention
** '''Sir Tiffy Cashien:''' spanned adventurers off joining, what?
** '''Player:''' You want me to be a squire for five years?!?!
** '''Sir Tiffy Cashien:''' Haw Haw Haw! No, no, goodness me, no!
** '''Sir Tiffy Cashien:''' Five years is a very long period of time nowadays - ANYTHING could happen in that time, and we need capable heroes like yourself as soon as possible.
** '''Sir Tiffy Cashien:''' No, I had a bit of a chat with Sir Vey, and we came up with... A different solution to the problem. Assuming you're still interested of course.
** {{tselect|Start the Wanted! quest?}}
** {{topt|Yes.}}
*** '''Player:''' I'm still up for joining the Temple Knights, I just don't really feel like spending five years running around shining peoples{{sic}} boots for them.
*** '''Sir Tiffy Cashien:''' Haw Haw Haw!
*** '''Sir Tiffy Cashien:''' I quite understand, what? No, don't worry, we were doing a little research into the White Knight Charter, and found an interesting loophole, what?
*** '''Player:''' Loophole? What kind of loophole?
*** '''Sir Tiffy Cashien:''' Well, you don't need to worry about the details, you just do as I tell you and it will all work out for us both, what?
*** '''Player:''' I guess... I don't really like blindly following orders though...
*** {{tselect|Select an option}}
*** {{topt|Ask about the Wanted! Quest}}
**** {{tact|below}}
*** {{topt|Ask about buying armour|quest=no.}}
*** {{topt|Can I switch respawns, please?|quest=no}}
** {{topt|No.}}
*** '''Player:''' No, to be honest I'm getting sick of all these excuses and procrastination. Plus being an inititiate{{sic}} was nowhere near as fun as I thought it would be.
*** '''Player:''' I'd rather just go off by myself and kill stuff for cash.
*** '''Sir Tiffy Cashien:''' Well, sorry to hear you say that old [boy/gal/bean], but I can't hold it against you.
*** '''Sir Tiffy Cashien:''' You will of course still be entitled to all that we can provide you with at an initiate level, but sadly you will never advance beyond that in our order. Was there anything you wanted?
*** {{tselect|Select an option}}
*** {{topt|Can I buy some armour?|quest=no}}
*** {{topt|Can I switch respawns please?|quest=no}}
*** {{topt|Goodbye.|quest=no}}

===Continuing the dialogue===
* {{topt|Ask about the Wanted! Quest}}
** '''Player:''' So what exactly do you want me to do?
** '''Sir Tiffy Cashien:''' Well now, it's really very simple. I want you to go to Sir Amik, tell him that you have decided to not join the Temple Knights, and that you have decided to become a White Knight instead.
** '''Sir Tiffy Cashien:''' He will then offer you to join as a squire; You will then decline his offer, and ask if you can be deputised instead.
** '''Player:''' Okaaaay....
** '''Sir Tiffy Cashien:''' If you run into any problems with that, come and see me.
** {{tselect|Select an option}}
** {{topt|How will all that help?}}
*** '''Player:''' I don't exactly understand how that will help me become a White Knight...
*** '''Sir Tiffy Cashien:''' Ah, your curiosity does you credit old [boy/gal/bean]! Let me tell you a little history lesson;
*** '''Sir Tiffy Cashien:''' Many centuries ago, the founders of the White Knights realised that in times of crisis, a long waiting period for new Knights could be disastrous for the kingdom, so they added a clause to the founding charter that would
*** '''Sir Tiffy Cashien:''' allow any citizen who has performed an act in the name of the White Knights to become deputised on a purely temporary basis to a full-fledged White Knight.
*** '''Player:''' So how does that affect me?
*** '''Sir Tiffy Cashien:''' Well now, your actions in the Black Knights' Fortress on behalf of the White Knights make you eligible to be deputised.
*** '''Player:''' But if that's only temporary, and I have to be a 'proper' White Knight to then become a Temple Knight, doesn't that mean that I am still going to have to squire for Amik for five years?
*** '''Sir Tiffy Cashien:''' Ah, well this is where the beauty of the plan lies, dontchaknow?
*** '''Sir Tiffy Cashien:''' Once you have been deputised, for the time that you are still working for their order, you are subject to all of the same rules and regulations that normal White Knights are, which means you are also eligible for
*** '''Sir Tiffy Cashien:''' battlefield promotions.
*** '''Player:''' I... don't understand...
*** '''Sir Tiffy Cashien:''' Let me put it like this; As a deputy you will be considered the lowest possible rank of White Knight, and may be removed entirely from their order at a whim.
*** '''Sir Tiffy Cashien:''' However, should you achieve some great feat while serving as a White Knight that you would be eligible for a promotion from, then by their own rules you would then have to be raised to a higher level within their
*** '''Sir Tiffy Cashien:''' order, and it would therefore become impossible to remove your rank, or make you no longer a deputy.
*** '''Player:''' So I get to be a White Knight without having to do five years of pointless busywork?
*** '''Sir Tiffy Cashien:''' Indeed. We Temple Knights have our reputation for a reason, dontchaknow?
*** '''Player:''' Okay, I guess that makes sense... But we're not in a time of crisis, so doesn't that mean I won't actually get deputised?
*** '''Sir Tiffy Cashien:''' Ah, do not concern yourself with THAT old [boy/gal/bean]; Crisis is such a subjective term, and as you will find out when you join us fully in the Temple Knights, there is always some potential crisis or other brewing.
*** '''Sir Tiffy Cashien:''' If we weren't as good at our jobs as we were, almost every day would be a day of crisis!
*** '''Sir Tiffy Cashien:''' All we really need to do is allow the old White Knights to handle a problem that we would normally deal with, and that should be a sufficient crisis to allow you to be deputised, dontchaknow.
*** {{tact|other}}
** {{topt|Do I really have to quit the Temple Knights?}}
*** '''Player:''' But... Do I really need to quit the Temple Knights?
*** '''Player:''' You seem pretty cool, and I really like the armour...
*** '''Sir Tiffy Cashien:''' Haw Haw Haw!
*** '''Sir Tiffy Cashien:''' No, not at all, this is merely a ruse; Sir Amik knows full well that his authority over our organisation is limited, so he will not deputise you unless he thinks that you are entirely unaffiliated with us.
*** '''Sir Tiffy Cashien:''' You are simply going to tell him that you have decided not to join us so that he will in turn deputise you to join the White Knights! We of course still want you to join us, it is just a
*** '''Sir Tiffy Cashien:''' little... misdirection.
*** {{tact|other}}
** {{topt|What am I supposed to be doing again?}}
*** {{tselect|Select an option}}
*** {{topt|Ask about the Wanted! Quest}}
**** '''Player:''' What am I supposed to be doing again?
**** '''Sir Tiffy Cashien:''' You are to go to Sir Amik Varze, leader of the White Knights of Falador, and are to tell him that you have decided not to join the Temple Knights.
**** '''Sir Tiffy Cashien:''' We will send him a messenger confirming this. He will offer you the opportunity to become his squire, you are to decline, and ask if you can be deputised instead.
**** '''Sir Tiffy Cashien:''' If you run into any problems with that, you are then to come and see me for further advice.
**** '''Sir Tiffy Cashien:''' Understood?
**** '''Player:''' Um, yeah, I think so...
**** {{tact|end}}
*** {{topt|Ask about buying armour.|quest=no}}
*** {{topt|Can I switch respawns, please?|quest=no}}


==Falador Castle: First visit to Sir Amik==
* '''Player:''' Hello Sir Amik.
* '''Sir Amik Varze:''' Hello, friend!
* {{tcond|If the player has not asked Tiffy about his plan:}}
** '''Sir Amik Varze:''' Well, I did have something you may have been interested in, but I've been given orders not to approach you for trivial matters now that you are a member of the Temple Knights.
** '''Player:''' Aaaaawwwww...
** {{tact|end}}
* '''Player:''' Got any jobs for me to do today?
* '''Sir Amik Varze:''' Well, I did have something you may have been interested in, but I've been given orders not to-
* '''Player:''' Can I just stop you right there?
* '''Player:''' I am no longer a member of the Temple Knights, I have entirely renounced my application because after many hours of soul searching I have come to the conclusion that I desperately want to become a White
* '''Player:''' Knight instead!
* {{tcond|If the player is wearing Initiate Armour:}}
** '''Sir Amik Varze:''' You don't want to be a Temple Knight anymore?
** '''Player:''' That is correct, yes.
** '''Sir Amik Varze:''' But you are wearing their armour!
** '''Player:''' So? Did you hear me bad mouth the armour? The armour is cool, I keep the armour!
** {{tact|continues}}
* '''Sir Amik Varze:''' I'm not sure I understand... You wish to desert the Temple Knights in favour of my own humble White Knights?
* '''Player:''' Absolutely!
* '''Player:''' And this is definitely not some kind of elaborate hoax to get my application processed faster.
* '''Sir Amik Varze:''' I'm sorry, did you say something just then?
* '''Player:''' No... Not if you didn't hear it...
* '''Sir Amik Varze:''' ... Well anyway, for the fine work you achieved at that incident in the Black Knights Fortress, I would be honoured to accept you as my Squire.
* '''Sir Amik Varze:''' So what do you say?
* {{tselect|Select an option}}
* {{topt|What does being a Squire entail?}}
* '''Player:''' So what exactly does being a squire consist of, then?
* '''Sir Amik Varze:''' You will spend the next five years of your life running various errands for me.
* '''Sir Amik Varze:''' If I consider you to have done a more than adequate job of this, then I will begin to consider possibly moving your name forwards to becoming a full-fledged member of the Order of the White Knights.
* '''Player:''' So... No killing stuff for you, or anything fun like that...?
* '''Sir Amik Varze:''' Not as such, no. Unless you consider killing time by running errands fun...?
* '''Player:''' Well, erm...
* '''Sir Amik Varze:''' So what say you [player name]? Spend five long years of your life doing pointless busywork without pay for me, on the off chance that at some point in the future I may put your name forward
* '''Sir Amik Varze:''' as a novice White Knight?
** {{tact|other}}
* {{topt|Yes please!}}
** '''Player:''' Yes please! I would LOVE to be your squire!
** '''Player:''' Wait... Didn't Sir Tiffy tell me to decline...?
** '''Player:''' Nah, Squire me up, Amik!
** '''Sir Amik Varze:''' As you wish, from this day forth you are my Squire!
** {{tact|end}}
* {{topt|No, not right now...}}
** '''Player:''' Um... As tempting an offer as that sounds Sir Amik, I am really not a fan of waiting around...
** '''Player:''' Now, I heard from some completely random stranger that was definitely not Sir Tiffy Cashien as part of an elaborate ruse to fast track my application into the White Knights, that I could be deputised directly as a
** '''Player:''' White Knight, and entirely bypass that whole boring waiting for five years thing...
** '''Sir Amik Varze:''' That is entirely correct [player name], but I have no idea where you may have heard that, for it is a secret guarded only to members of our order!
** '''Player:''' Right. Well anyway, can I do that instead?
** '''Sir Amik Varze:''' Well, a fine adventurer such as yourself would be a perfect candidate as a deputy in my eyes, but fortunately this can only be done in a time of crisis, and all is currently well.
** '''Player:''' All is well, huh? I'll be right back, I just have to go and ask...
** '''Player:''' nobody in particular if they can organise... nothing at all to happen.
** '''Sir Amik Varze:''' You are a strange one [player name]...
** {{tact|end}}

===Talking to Sir Amik after refusing to become his squire===
* '''Player:''' Hello Sir Amik.
* '''Sir Amik Varze:''' Hello, friend!
* '''Player:''' Got any jobs for me to do today?
* '''Sir Amik Varze:''' Only to become my Squire. Do you wish to become my squire?
* '''Player:''' No, not really. So there isn't a crisis yet?
* '''Sir Amik Varze:''' Thank Saradomin, no! We have not had a crisis for many years now!
* '''Player:''' Right. Well, I'll go and see if Tiffy can fix that for me then.
* '''Player:''' Er, I mean: How fortunate for us all that nothing terrible has happened or is conveniently about to happen.
* '''Sir Amik Varze:''' Indeed!
* {{tact|end}}

===Talking to Sir Amik after becoming his squire===
* '''Player:''' Hello Sir Amik.
* '''Sir Amik Varze:''' Hello, friend!
* '''Player:''' So do you have any squiring for me today Amik?
* '''Sir Amik Varze:''' Yes, yes in fact I do. I would like you to bring me an Asgarnian Ale.
* '''Sir Amik Varze:''' No matured Ale, no other brand, simply an Asgarnian Ale.
* '''Player:''' Okay boss.
* '''Sir Amik Varze:''' That is 'Sir Amik' or 'My Liege' – not 'Boss'.
* '''Player:''' Gotcha, boss.
* {{tact|end}}

===Returning with Asgarnian Ale===
* '''Player:''' Hello Sir. Amik
* '''Sir Amik Varze:''' Hello Friend
* '''Player:''' Hi boss.
* '''Sir Amik Varze:''' Call me Sir Amik, or liege.
* '''Player:''' Sure thing, boss. I brought you a beer.
* '''Player:''' Anything else you want boss?
* '''Sir Amik Varze:''' Well, another Asgarnian Ale would be greatly appreciated. And stop calling me Boss.
* '''Player:''' Sure thing boss!
* {{tact|end}}

==Falador Park: The Crisis==
===Talking to Sir Tiffy after agreeing to be Amik's Squire===
* '''Player:''' I did it Tiffy! I became Sir Amik's squire!
* '''Player:''' That means in just five short years I can be a White Knight!
* '''Sir Tiffy Cashien:''' ...What? I told you to decline!
* '''Player:''' Yeeeesssssss.... But I thought it would be more fun to do this?
* '''Sir Tiffy Cashien:''' *sigh* This is a less than illustrious start to your career with us [player name].
* '''Sir Tiffy Cashien:''' Never mind, all is not lost, I have sent word to Amik that a dangerous criminal we once thought exiled is on the loose again, and that he should send all available White Knights to confront him.
* '''Sir Tiffy Cashien:''' This should give him enough of a scare to deputise you immediately.
* '''Sir Tiffy Cashien:''' Go and speak to Amik again, and then immediately come back here, we will need to prepare you for your mission.
* {{tact|end}}

===Talking to Sir Tiffy after declining to be Amik's Squire===
* {{tselect|Select an option}}
* {{topt|Ask about the Wanted! Quest}}
** '''Player:''' Hello again Tiffy. I've just spoken to Amik, and he says he's fine for me to be deputised as a White Knight, there just needs to be a crisis first.
** '''Player:''' I assume you can arrange a small crisis for me?
** '''Sir Tiffy Cashien:''' Haw Haw Haw, fitting right in with the Temple Knight way of thinking, what?
** '''Sir Tiffy Cashien:''' Well, as a matter of fact, I will not have to organise anything, there is a particularly vicious and dangerous criminal currently at loose!
** '''Sir Tiffy Cashien:''' I have already notified Sir Amik through the usual channels, so just go and speak to him quickly, then pop back here and we'll get you equipped for the hunt, what?
** '''Player:''' You know... Is all this back and forth strictly necessary?
** '''Player:''' I don't mean to sound ungrateful for the help you're giving me here, but you could have just got this sorted out before sending me off there in the first place!
** '''Sir Tiffy Cashien:''' Ah, yes, well most awfully sorry about all the running around you've been doing old bean, but when it comes to our line of work, sometimes the indirect route is the best, what?
** '''Player:''' I don't understand...?
** '''Player:''' And stop calling me bean! I am not a vegetable, I am a human bean, er, being!
** '''Sir Tiffy Cashien:''' Awfully sorry dear heart, it's just a term of affection, what? Anyway...
** '''Sir Tiffy Cashien:''' This criminal is a very dangerous fellow, and has some very dangerous friends.
** '''Sir Tiffy Cashien:''' If he has no reason to suspect you to be working for us, then he will be a little sloppier than he otherwise might be, because he will just assume you to be one of those stupid White Knights.
** '''Sir Tiffy Cashien:''' We want this man caught, for the good of the country, and if we need to fool a few people into thinking you're nothing to do with us, and you have to do a little extra walking, then that's what is going to happen, what?
** '''Player:''' I guess... But this spy stuff is a lot more boring than it sounded at first...
** {{tact|end}}
* {{topt|Ask about buying armour.|quest=no}}
* {{topt|Can I switch respawns, please?|quest=no}}

===Talking to Sir Tiffy before revisiting Sir Amik===
* {{tselect|Select an option}}
* {{topt|Ask about the Wanted! Quest}}
** '''Player:''' Hi Tiffy. What am I supposed to be doing again?
** '''Sir Tiffy Cashien:''' Go and report to Sir Amik for 'orders'. You will be unsurprised to find out he will now be prepared to deputise you.
** '''Sir Tiffy Cashien:''' After you have spoken to him return here immediately, your life will be at risk without our assistance, and we don't want you dying on your first mission for us, what?
** {{tact|end}}
* {{topt|Ask about buying armour.|quest=no}}
* {{topt|Can I switch respawns, please?|quest=no}}

==Falador Castle: Second visit to Sir Amik==
* '''Player:''' Hello Sir Amik.
* '''Sir Amik Varze:''' Hello, friend!
* '''Sir Amik Varze:''' Thank Saradomin you have come back here!
* '''Sir Amik Varze:''' We have received word from one of our scouts that the evil Solus Dellagar has returned to Asgarnia!
* '''Sir Amik Varze:''' What is worse, it seems he is in possession of dangerous new magics that we are powerless against!
* '''Sir Amik Varze:''' Please, I implore you in the name of all that is holy, assist us in banishing him from our kingdom once more!
* '''Sir Amik Varze:''' I cannot bear to think of the troubles he may bring us...
* {{tselect|Select an option}}
* {{topt|Who is Solus?}}
** '''Player:''' Solus Dellagar? Who - or what - is that?
** '''Sir Amik Varze:''' You have not heard of the infamous murder-mage? He terrorised these lands many years past, thinking himself above the law with his powerful enchantments, but the White Knights finally managed to bring him to
** '''Sir Amik Varze:''' justice and he was permanently exiled.
** '''Player:''' Exiled? Why didn't you just kill him? Or, you know, imprison him or whatever?
** '''Sir Amik Varze:''' Kill an unarmed foe? That is not the way of Saradomin, nor of the White Knights.
** '''Sir Amik Varze:''' As for imprisonment... Solus is a highly dangerous man not just because of his mastery of the magical arts, but for his uncanny resourcefulness.
** '''Sir Amik Varze:''' To tell you the truth, I fear that I would be unable to guarantee his captivity in any holding cell belonging to us...
** '''Player:''' So if you can't imprison him, and exile obviously didn't work, you want me to kill him?
** '''Sir Amik Varze:''' I did not say that. I did not say that at all. That is against all of our codes of honour.
** '''Sir Amik Varze:''' However, should you find yourself in combat with him, and there is no other way, then perhaps for him to die would be best for us all.
** '''Sir Amik Varze:''' You understand me, [player name]?
** '''Player:''' Oh yes. You've made yourself very clear.
** '''Sir Amik Varze:''' So will you aid us in this fight?
** {{tact|other}}
* {{topt|What will I get for helping?}}
** '''Player:''' So what will I get if I help you out against this, er, solus doolalala guy then?
** '''Sir Amik Varze:''' Why, you will help keep Asgarnia free of malicious influence, and perform a good deed in the name of King Vallance and of the White Knights!
** '''Player:''' Yes, yes I see. So... No monetary compensation or other actual reward then?
** '''Sir Amik Varze:''' As Saradomin has told us, 'a good deed is its own reward'.
** '''Player:''' So I don't actually get anything out of this then?
** '''Sir Amik Varze:''' Nothing tangible, no, but you will be deputized to act as a White Knight, and you will feel a warm glow inside of having done the right thing.
** '''Player:''' But you can't buy things with a warm glow...
** '''Sir Amik Varze:''' So what say you [player name]? Fight with honour in the name of the White Knights against the terrible Solus?
** {{tact|other}}
* {{topt|Sure, I'll help you!}}
** '''Player:''' Hey, there's nothing I like more than fighting! Deputise me up, and I'll go get this guy for you!
** '''Sir Amik Varze:''' Very well then; In the name of King Valence,{{sic}} and for the honour of Saradomin, I now pronounce you a fully deputised White Knight.
** '''Sir Amik Varze:''' May honour and glory follow you in every action.
** '''Player:''' So where should I start looking for this Solus guy anyway?
** '''Sir Amik Varze:''' I haven't the faintest idea. Good luck!
** {{tact|end}}
* {{topt|I don't feel like helping you right now.}}
** '''Player:''' A scary mage huh? Sounds like I could get KILLED!
** '''Player:''' Forget that, and forget you! No way am I risking my neck unless there's a big fat reward on the table for it!
** '''Player:''' And sometimes not even then...
** '''Sir Amik Varze:''' It is a tragedy to hear you speak so, but we must trust in our valour and the wisdom of Saradomin to protect us from this evil man if we cannot enlist help against him.
** {{tact|end}}

===Talking to Sir Amik after agreeing to go after Solus===
* '''Player:''' Hello Sir Amik.
* '''Sir Amik Varze:''' Hello, friend!
* '''Sir Amik Varze:''' [player name]... Solus Dellagar is still loose... Please, for the safety of my lands you must find him immediately...
* '''Player:''' Any hints on where he might be?
* '''Sir Amik Varze:''' We have no idea where he might be now... His magic is too powerful for us, I do not know how to stop him...
* '''Player:''' Hum. I wonder if Sir Tiffy might be able to help?
* {{tact|end}}

==Falador Park: Mission details==
* {{tselect|Select an option}}
* {{topt|Ask about the Wanted! Quest}}
** '''Player:''' Tiffy, it worked exactly to plan! Sir Amik deputised me to take care of this Solus Doolally dude, so let's go get him!
** '''Sir Tiffy Cashien:''' His name is Solus Dellagar, and honestly, he is one of the most dangerous men in Gielinor.
** '''Sir Tiffy Cashien:''' Not only is he extremely adept at magic, he is also quite prepared to use that magic at a moments{{sic}} notice, because he is quite, quite mad.
** '''Player:''' So... Dragonhide armour and an elemental shield and I'm laughing?
** '''Sir Tiffy Cashien:''' No, no, no. Listen to me [boy/girl/kid]; You are under NO CIRCUMSTANCES to engage him directly in combat!
** '''Sir Tiffy Cashien:''' You are to act as our agent and track him down, when you have managed to corner him somewhere then we will send in a field recovery team directly to take him away without incident.
** '''Sir Tiffy Cashien:''' I cannot stress this enough; You are to observe and locate, you are NOT to enter a combat situation!
** '''Player:''' Riiiiight... So I'm just going to scout him out for you then.
** '''Player:''' Any tips on how to find him?
** '''Sir Tiffy Cashien:''' Well old bean, we will need to equip you for the task, but you'll need to get something for me first, what?
** '''Player:''' What kind of stuff?
** '''Sir Tiffy Cashien:''' Well, we teach our operatives the value of their equipment by making them pay for it, what?
** '''Sir Tiffy Cashien:''' You have two choices here, you can either give me cash directly, and I will hand it over, or you can bring me the raw materials and I will make you one.
** {{tselect|What would you like to do?}}

====Dossier of Solus Dellagar====
CLASSIFIED

{{colour|red|Solus Dellagar}}<br/>

{{colour|blue|Age:}}<br/>
Unknown.<br/>
{{colour|blue|Place of Birth:}}<br/>
Unknown.<br/>
{{colour|blue|Known aliases:}}<br/>
Solus Darkheart<br/>
The Murder-mage<br/>
'Mad Solus'<br/>
Stealthy Pete<br/>
{{colour|blue|Known affiliates:}}<br/>
Solus Dellagar has shown time and time again that he<br/>
considers others to be mere pawns in his schemes, and will<br/>
discard them at the first viable opportunity.<br/>
Despite having been associated with many criminal and<br/>
undesirable elements known to us, these will not be listed<br/>
as affiliates, because as a general rule, if you have<br/>
worked with Solus once you are unlikely to ever do so<br/>
again.<br/>
The only loyalty he has ever managed to inspire in others<br/>
is through threat of force, and he is indeed powerful, but<br/>
the general hatred of him amongst those he has<br/>
encountered means that an experienced field operative<br/>
will find opportunities to turn associates against him.<br/>
{{colour|blue|Known History:}}<br/>
Solus' exact history is still unknown to us, but we suspect<br/>
he originated in or close to the city of Ardougne.

He was first brought to our attention as a possible threat<br/>
in the infamous zombie attack of Varrock masterminded<br/>
by the Mahjarrat Lucien, but did not serve a particularly<br/>
key role.

Reports of his whereabouts after that are somewhat<br/>
sketchy, but he seems to have trained a quite formidable<br/>
magical aptitude in the decades immediately following.

Although he has kept a low profile from conventional<br/>
authorities, he has made quite a name for himself<br/>
amongst various underworld circles, especially amongst<br/>
Zamorakians, where his particularly brutal method have<br/>
been cause from some concern.

He earned the nickname 'Murder-mage' and 'Mad Solus' in<br/>
the incident at Edgeville where he was eventually<br/>
apprehended by one of our field teams, but not after the<br/>
wilful{{sic}} slaughter of over 800 civilians, as well as an equal<br/>
number of White and Black Knights - we are still unsure as<br/>
to why Lord Daquarius allowed his men to be involved in<br/>
this affair ,{{sic}} because it was distinctly against his usual<br/>
methods, and this is the only report on file of him making<br/>
an action under someone else's direct command.

Solus' reputation as an evil, bloodthirsty, greedy and<br/>
dangerous individual is well deserved, and field<br/>
operatives should avoid direct confrontation at all costs.

Standard observation rules apply, and if you find<br/>
yourself in a position where confrontation seems likely,<br/>
then guidelines suggest you immediately contact your<br/>
handler who will provide you ample backup - your chances<br/>
of surviving a one on one assault are slim to none.

End of Report.

====Dossier of Lord Daquarius====
CLASSIFIED

{{colour|red|Lord Daquarius}}<br/>

{{colour|blue|Age:}}<br/>
34.<br/>
{{colour|blue|Place of Birth:}}<br/>
Falador.<br/>
{{colour|blue|Known aliases:}}<br/>
Lord of the Kinshra<br/>
Daquarius Rennard<br/>
{{colour|blue|Known affiliates:}}<br/>
Leader of the Kinshra, commonly known as the Black<br/>
Knights.<br/>
Has occasional ties to various other Zamorakian agencies.<br/>
Has been linked with the Witch Lensig and her familiar<br/>
Greebo{{sic|Greldo, not Greebo}} most recently.<br/>
Has a number of jail guard in his employ deep in the<br/>
Taverley dungeon, where enemies of the Kinshra are often<br/>
imprisoned.<br/>
{{colour|blue|Known History:}}<br/>
The charismatic Lord Daquarius was the youngest Black<br/>
Knight to ever take lead of the Kinshra, being unanimously<br/>
voted into leadership after the death of Lord Shadwell in<br/>
the infamous incident at Edgeville.<br/>

As leader of the Kinshra, he has been a high priority<br/>
threat to the White Knights, and his activities with the<br/>
Black Knights have been a constant thorn in both the side<br/>
of the White Knights and of the Temple Knights.<br/>

However, while the White Knights still actively seek his<br/> 
capture and execution for crimes against the state,<br/>
the Temple Knights have taken a more reactive position of<br/>
observation.<br/>

Those of us who survived the Edgeville incident and recall<br/>
what the Black Knights activities under Lord Shadwell were<br/>
like, can see that Lord Daquarius is better to keep around<br/>
than risk another fanatical extremist taking his place.<br/>

For all of his misguided belief in Zamorak, Daquarius is an<br/>
undeniably noble man; we have numerous reports of him<br/>
risking personal injury so that he may save a fellow<br/>
Kinshra from harm or death.<br/>

His belief in his men as more than simply subjects to be<br/>
used in war against the White Knights makes him a<br/>
predictable and easily manipulated enemy that is worth<br/>
keeping in place, and also accounts for the high regard<br/>
in which he is held by the rest of the Kinshra.<br/>

End of Report.

====Dossier of Zamorakian Research Mage====
CLASSIFIED

{{colour|red|Name Unknown}}<br/>

{{colour|blue|Age:}}<br/>
Unknown.<br/>

Unknown.<br/>

{{colour|blue|Known affiliates:}}<br/>
The Zamorakian Magical Institute, a research group that<br/> 
we have classified as fairly innocuous that primarily<br/>
focuses on magical research dedicated to assisting<br/>
Zamorak.<br/>
Observation suggests that the Z.M.I. is the same faction<br/>
of Zamorakians that burnt down the Wizards{{sic}} Tower in<br/>
Operation: Phoenix, but firm conclusions as to the reason<br/>
for this remain at best sketchy and unsupported by<br/>
evidence.<br/>
It is certainly worthwhile to keep any known members of<br/>
the Z.M.I. under observation, however.<br/>
{{colour|blue|Known History:}}<br/>
Recently this unidentified mage has begun to base his<br/>
activities in and around the area of Varrock, specifically<br/>
the Temple to Zamorak that was foolishly allowed to be<br/>
built there.<br/>

We have some evidence that this Mage also works as a<br/>
rune-dealer in the vicinity of Edgeville, but preventing his<br/>
operations in the Wilderness is far beyond our<br/>
jurisdiction, and any actions taken there would bring<br/>
unwanted attention to our own order by various entities.<br/>

We have installed standard observation devices in the<br/>
Zamorakian temple, but his activities have apparently<br/>
been limited to a small degree of smuggling and the<br/>
purchasing and resale of various pieces of contraband.<br/>

Although no obvious threat from his presence has been<br/>
detected, we will continue standard observation in case he<br/>
turns out to be a bigger fish than he at first glance<br/>
seems.<br/>

End of Report.

Transcript:Waterlogged journal
content:
{{Transcript|item}}

===Entry 1===
The fall of the Wizards' Tower should have been a turning point for the Order of Wizards. We had the canvas wiped clean, with the ability to start fresh with no prejudices or preconceived notions of what a wizard should be. We could have entered a golden age of magic founded on the basis that nobody can control what magic is, or what it should be.

Instead, the wizards in charge decided to rebuild the exact same tower with the exact same problems.

I heard rumours that the Saradominists in the Order burned the tower down when they were trying to steal the work of the Zamorakians. Others claimed it was the Zamorakians themselves that did it. In truth, the different sects of the Order were butting heads to the point where conflict was inevitable. The Tower was always destined to fall. This new one, I suspect, will eventually suffer the same fate.

I will be a part of it no longer. I'm leaving to make my own future, free from the infighting of these so-called wizards.

===Entry 2===
I have found myself in the company of some pirates on the Pandemonium. While the law may consider some of their activities barbaric, their camaraderie has been aspirational. Nobody cares who you are or what you've done in a past life. All that matters is that you take care of your own.

I've decided to join them on their next voyage. They are of course no stranger to discovering new lands and ancient treasures. Indeed, they've likely covered every inch of land above the waters' edge. But what of below?

There could be a whole host of mysteries beneath the surface of the water, just waiting to be discovered. All this crew needs is a wizard to help them explore the places that they alone can't reach.

===Entry 3===
I have spent many months perfecting what I'm calling the Medallion of the Deep. Being removed from the Order of Wizards means also being removed from their libraries. Once, creating new magics was often a collaborative process eventually resulting in a perfect outcome. Now, things are slightly less refined. However, I am most pleased with the end result. With this medallion, the treasures of the depths will soon be ours.

===Entry 4===
It seems I have created an effigy of failure. When we made it to open waters, the Captain (I shall not sully this journal with his name) turned on me and tried to take the Medallion for himself. In his eyes, I saw the same greed, the same jealousy that I had seen in my peers. It was the very thing that brought the Wizards' Tower to rubble.

With no other choice, I combatted the Captain and the rest of the crew and emerged victorious, though I was brought within inches of my life. In the fighting, the Medallion of the Deep that they all craved so desperately was torn asunder, its pieces falling off the deck and into the depths below. For all that I thought I could write my own future, I too could only create destruction.

===Entry 5===
Alone at sea, it wasn't long before the authorities found me. This cell in Rock Island Prison is now my home, this journal now my only possession. Having seen the world at its worst, I thought this an acceptable end, but cruel fate was not disposed of me yet. In my experiments in creating the Medallion of the Deep, some part of me was imbued into it, and hence, some part of me was now buried in its fragments.

Since my arrival here, I have been plagued by what many would call visions, but nightmares would be a more fitting name. Having had many moons to disseminate them in my mind, I believe these nightmares to be of the resting places of each of the eight pieces of the Medallion of the Deep.

In the first nightmare, I am shut firmly within a rusted chest, slowly asphyxiating in solitude while the wind pushes through palm trees and the ocean laps the shores around me.

In the second nightmare, I am buried under the waves, tanged in coral, drowning in perpetuity in the seas I had hoped to call my own.

In the third nightmare, I am held captive by those not even the Pandemonium would take in, constrained by their greed and malice over black sands.

In the fourth nightmare, I am held by a small animal in a field of shining rocks, but with no food in sight to sate its hunger.

In the fifth nightmare, I am placed among a tray of silver in a market on the seas, doomed to rot amongst those shinier than I.

In the sixth nightmare, I am sat atop the tallest trees on an uninhabited island, forced to endure the elements at their most potent.

In the seventh nightmare, I am submerged in acidic liquid, burning, scalding forever, while the rattle of bones echoes in the night. Creatures of my own  creation? I hope not.

In the final nightmare, I know not where I am. All I can hear is the infernal, rhythmic clicking of a hundred different creatures, all in the same pattern. This is the worst nightmare. The rhythm lingers even when I wake.

If I had the strength and the freedom of my jailors, I could use these visions to find and reassemble the Medallion. However, my fate is already sealed. Instead, I plan to cast this journal into the waves. Most likely it will be lost forever, but if it is not and if someone is reading this now, the knowledge of the Medallion of the Deep is now yours. However, if you do decide to attempt to reassemble it, be warned, for greed is a powerful foe. May my fate be a clear reminder of that.

~W.S.

{{Colour|#1e1e1e|*The last few pages are rough diagrams of the shape and construction of the Medallion. You feel reasonably confident that if you had the fragments of it, you could reassemble it by hand.*}}

title: Transcript:Weave
Transcript:Weird Old Man
Transcript:Weiss fire notes
content:
{{Transcript|item}}

==={{Colour|#7f0000|Salts}}===
The salts found in the caves around Weiss are fascinating. By burning them in the correct proportions, I can achieve incredible effects.

Some combinations can counter the effects of cold weather, others can dispel darkness more effectively than any natural light source, and some seem able to imbue the rocks of the cave with magical-looking powers!

The challenge for me has been identifying the correct proportions. And, of course, finding suitable places to use them - my age makes it hard for me to explore beyond the boundaries of Weiss these days.

Perhaps other combinations will be discovered in future, with even more helpful applications. Knowledge is valuable in itself, but that dolt Mother values only inventions that help him fight.

==={{Colour|#7f0000|Braziers}}===
We trolls have never been skilled at Construction, and I get little opportunity to practice here.

However, from my calculations, I believe the optimal site for my fires would be a brazier constructed from {{Colour|#272727|steel}} and {{Colour|#3f2f1f|mahogany}}. Two metal bars and two planks should suffice to construct the frame.

One should then be able to ignite the salts in the brazier to get the desired effect.

==={{Colour|#7f0000|Fire of Eternal Light}}===
This was one of the easiest fires to invent; by burning a stack of {{Colour|#7f0000|300 Te Salt}}, {{Colour|#00007f|100 Efh Salt}} and {{Colour|#003600|50 Urt Salt}}, I produced a flame that lit up my entire cave.

Its light shone more brightly than any torch or lantern I have seen, and as far as I can tell it shows no sign of ever burning out.

==={{Colour|#7f0000|Fire of Nourishment}}===
Although we are surrounded by trees, related to the pine family, and there are a few pale flowers, little else seems to grow here. I originally believed this was due to the cold, and I invented the Fire of Nourishment to counteract it.

The fire requires {{Colour|#7f0000|50 Te Salt}}, {{Colour|#00007f|100 Efh Salt}} and {{Colour|#003600|150 Urt Salt}}.

Unfortunately, I later found that the soil around Weiss is barren and unsuitable for crops. Mother called my work a complete waste of time - he cannot grasp that this knowledge may be useful in future, even if he can't use it right now.

He is such a limited ruler!

==={{Colour|#7f0000|Fire of Unseasonal Warmth}}===
Living in the cold mountains, I naturally turned my attention to the matter of keeping warm, and succeeded beyond all expectations!

By burning a stack of {{Colour|#7f0000|100 Te Salt}}, {{Colour|#00007f|50 Efh Salt}} and {{Colour|#003600|300 Urt Salt}}, I produced a flame that completely dispelled the chill of the weather.

In some parts of the mountains, the cold is so intense that one loses all one's abilities. I feel sure that my Fire of Unseasonal Warmth would render one completely immune to that problem.

==={{Colour|#7f0000|Fire of Dehumidification}}===
I stumbled upon this one by accident. A stack of {{Colour|#7f0000|50 Te Salt}}, {{Colour|#00007f|300 Efh Salt}} and {{Colour|#003600|100 Urt Salt}} burnt with a strange heat that dried out my cave - obviously fire should do that, but this one did it much faster than normal. I imagine that if one were to light this fire in a damp environment, it would provide protection from rotting effects and decay.

Maybe if I live long enough, I will find a way to travel the world and find such a place.

==={{Colour|#7f0000|Fire of Domination}}===
Mother was very pleased with me when I presented him the recipe for this fire. It gave him simply incredible powers in combat, rendering him almost immune to any damage!

I also noticed that it disrupted my experiments with the Glowing Basalt teleporters; this would be helpful for Mother if he wished to prevent a mage from fleeing via their teleport magicks.

The combination for this fire was extremely hard to get right, but I eventually -

Odd Mushroom's notes were damaged, and I cannot find the rest of this recipe. I fear it is lost forever. - Snowflake

==={{Colour|#7f0000|Glowing Basalt}}===
The basalt rocks beneath Weiss have been altered by the powers of the salts, probably over millennia. This means I can modify them further by treating them with carefully calibrated combinations of salts, achieving effects that - frankly - look indistinguishable from magic.

With the correct combination of salts, the basalt can be made to transport matter - rocks, logs, even living creatures like goats - from place to place.

Perhaps it truly is magic - it certainly acts like the teleport spells of which I have heard!

My pupil, Snowflake, has helped me greatly with these experiments. She is far more intelligent than her father, Mother. Perhaps she inherited her brains from her mother, not from Mother.

In fact Snowflake did most of the work on refining the destinations of our matter transporters. Maybe she's cleverer than me... but I won't tell her that yet.

There'll be plenty more time for us to chat - I'm not old enough to fear death yet.

Anyway, Snowflake worked out that {{Colour|#00007f|3 Efh Salt}} and {{Colour|#7f0000|1 Te Salt}} can make a matter transporter focused on the woods outside Weiss where she used to play, as a child.

Maybe she will invent more combinations for other destinations soon.

From what my darling My Arm has told me of his homeland, a dose of {{Colour|#003600|3 Urt Salt}} and {{Colour|#7f0000|1 Te Salt}} should direct the focus to the Troll Stronghold. - Snowflake

I saw Odd Mushroom invent many other fires, but I cannot find any more of his notes.

Perhaps Father destroyed them, not understanding their value. Or perhaps they are merely lost, and will be found again.

I shall continue to search when I can, or perhaps I will rediscover the secrets myself! If I do, I shall prepare an updated edition of this book for my friend [player name].

- Snowflake

title: Transcript:Welcome to Soul Wars!
content:
{{Transcript}}

[[File:Welcome to Soul Wars! (1).jpg]]

Soul Wars

Old School runescape's newest minigame

You might remember Soul Wars from 2009, when it first released in RuneScape. Since it was two years past the 2007 deadline, this minigame was passed over when it came to creating Old School RuneScape - but the community kept asking to see it, so we've brought it back!

Soul Wars is a competitive minigame where two teams face off to claim territory and defeat the other team's Avatar. The team with the most avatar kills at the end of the game are the declared the winners!

Eager to try it out? You'll need at least 40 combat, 500 total levels, and RuneScape membership to participate.

If you've got all that, then hop through the portal at Edgeville or Ferox Enclave to travel straight to the Isle of Souls, where you can get battling!

[[File:Welcome to Soul Wars! (2).jpg]]

PROVE YOUR PROWESS

Best your PvP opponents and prove that you're the superior fighter! The more skillfully you play, the more Zeal you'll earn!

REAP THE REWARDS

Spend your hard-earned Zeal Tokens on a variety of rewards, including the Soul Cape, the Ectoplasmator and even Lucky Dips!

[[File:Welcome to Soul Wars! (3).jpg]]

Want to try soul wars?

Become a member today!

Soul Wars is members-only content. Upgrade to membership to access Soul Wars and loads of other minigames, quests and skills.

Members get access to other exclusive content like members only-quests, skills and mini-games.

title: Transcript:Werewolf (Darkmeyer)
content:
{{Transcript|npc}}

==Standard dialogue==
===East of the Darkmeyer Meat Shop===
* '''Player:''' Hey!
* '''Werewolf:''' What?
* '''Player:''' What are you doing?
* '''Werewolf:''' Waiting.
* '''Player:''' For what?
* '''Werewolf:''' For you to go away.
* '''Player:''' Oh... okay.
* {{tact|end}}

===The Crypt===
* '''Werewolf:''' There's nothing good to drink here.
* '''Player:''' What's wrong with blood?
* '''Werewolf:''' Blood's only good if there's meat to go with it.
* '''Player:''' Why even come here if there's nothing for you to drink?
* '''Werewolf:''' I'm here on business.
* '''Player:''' What business?
* '''Werewolf:''' My business is none of your business. Go poke your nose somewhere else.
* {{tact|end}}

===Lord Myrmel's home===
====Before The Blood Moon Rises====
* '''Werewolf:''' Don't disturb me. I need to guard the tithes.
* '''Player:''' Why? Where would they even go if they escaped?
* '''Werewolf:''' Escape? I'm not here to stop them escaping. I'm here to stop them getting stolen.
* '''Player:''' Oh...
* '''Werewolf:''' Now take your stupid questions somewhere else. I have a job to do.
* {{tact|end}}

====After The Blood Moon Rises, initial dialogue====
* '''Werewolf:''' This town is so boring now. Want to spice things up a bit?
* '''Player:''' Spice things up?
* '''Werewolf:''' That's right. You look like someone who might like to kill a few vampyres.
* '''Player:''' If I wanted to kill vampyres, surely I could just do that?
* '''Werewolf:''' But there's no fun in that. You want to get them angry first! So angry that they just keep coming! I have a way.
* '''Player:''' That being?
* '''Werewolf:''' I've put together a little something. I call it a garlic cocktail. It's disgustingly potent, especially to a vampyre. The smell literally fills them with rage. Want to buy one?
* {{tselect|Select an option}}
* {{topt|Yes please.}}
** '''Player:''' Yes please.
** {{tact|opens=Garlic Cocktail Supply}}
* {{topt|No thanks.}}
** '''Player:''' No thanks.
** '''Werewolf:''' Clear off then.
** {{tact|end}}

====After The Blood Moon Rises, subsequent dialogue====
* '''Werewolf:''' Want to buy a garlic cocktail?
* {{tselect|Select an option}}
* {{topt|Yes please.}}
** {{tact|above}}
* {{topt|No thanks.}}
** {{tact|above}}

===If the player is not disguised===
* {{tact|'''Note:''' This dialogue is removed after the third fight against Lowerniel in The Blood Moon Rises.}}
* '''Werewolf:''' You shouldn't be here, slave. Go back to your master before you get yourself killed.
* {{tact|end}}
